tieu_de: Buddhism is Practice, Not Just Talk
tom_tat: Day and night are like arrows, years like a shuttle. Waves on the river, each wave pushes the previous wave; Beautiful scenery fades quickly. Young people's lives pass quickly, soon they will grow old and die, leaving no trace behind, it's enough to see how meaningless everything is...
noi_dung:
Buddhism is Practice, Not Just Talking

Ethics are the basics of being human.

Once we have morality, we can stand firm.

Day and night are like arrows, years like a shuttle. Waves on the river, each wave pushes the previous wave; Beautiful scenery fades quickly. Young people's lives pass quickly, soon they will grow old and die, leaving no trace behind. It is enough to see that everything is impermanent.

Because everything is impermanent, we must quickly find a place of refuge. You are very lucky, after searching and pursuing, you finally have faith in Buddha. Only by believing in Buddha can we reach the place of Permanence, Bliss, Self, and Pureness; That is, the ultimate joy. Therefore we must believe in Buddha. But just believing is not enough, we must practice according to the Dharma. If you believe but don't practice, it's like talking about eating, or counting money for others, but you don't feel full, or richer. That's why the ancients said:

The Tao is weak,

Is there any way to use it?

Virtue is essential to practice,

Not cultivating the principles of virtue?

Mean:

The Way must be practiced,

If you don't practice, why is it called Tao?

Duc by cultivating,

If you don't cultivate virtue, how can you become successful?

So we have to "practice,"actually practice. Often hang the two words of life and death between his eyebrows and the two words "morality" trampled under his feet. Saying it out loud sounds confusing. Why trample "morality" underfoot? Because morality is the root of being human, like the root of a tree. Only with morality can we stand firm, but conversely, without morality we are like a tree without roots, unable to stand. We need to put morality into practice so that our personality will be strong and everything we do will naturally be successful. Therefore: "Ethics are two words, they are the basic element." That means morality is the basis of being human. The book Analects says: "The gentleman cultivates the duty, the duty establishes the path of birth." That is, the gentleman pays attention to the root, when the root is strong, the Way arises. Taking care of the roots will give birth to the path. That is the wise teaching of the ancients.

As I said earlier, time flies by like an arrow without us even realizing it. The past has passed, but the future needs to be established and principles cannot be left to pass by in a blur.

Principles of Tay Lac Vien Pagoda is to promote Pure Land Dharma; advocate diligently reciting Buddha's name. Normally every year on June 19 and November 17 of the lunar calendar, the Pagoda celebrates the Avalokitesvara and That Di Da Dharma Assembly. But you can't just participate for the sake of it. This year we must be more diligent than last year, we must always be focused, during these seven days, every hour, every minute we must diligently recite the Bodhisattva's name without getting tired.

When reciting Bodhisattva, we should not expect Bodhisattva to reciting us. Why so? Because during the time of retreat, if you have the name of participating in retreat but do not diligently recite the holy names, and your heart is full of random thoughts, it will only make the great compassionate Bodhisattva feel sorry for you: That you were not sincere in retreat, that you are truly pitiful. Therefore, the masses must earnestly recite and develop compassion, joy and equanimity. If so, I confirm that Bodhisattva will definitely bless you.

In the past, Tay Lac Vien has never sent out invitations to attend the ceremony, but rather the public volunteered to attend. Such a spirit of spontaneous development is very good and deserves to be commended. But we must not let this sincerity go to waste, but must make a vow to chant until "water falls and rocks appear" meaning the water dries up and the rocks are exposed. Recite until the Bodhisattva appears and preaches the Dharma. So it's not a waste of time to participate in the battle.

Today is the first day of the Dharma conference. I hope you will reap many achievements this year. On the contrary, I will pay this debt to you. If this debt cannot be calculated, don't regret it! Okay, I won't joke with you anymore, just recite more Bodhisattva names!

Lectured on June 13, 1958, on the occasion of the Avalokitesvara Festival, Hong Kong

tieu_de: The Great Compassion Mantra Eliminates Accidents
tom_tat: Even when the weather is extremely hot, you are not afraid of the heat or the long distance to the high mountains. Is there any benefit to coming here to participate in a meditation retreat? True benefit is often difficult to express. Like a drinker…
noi_dung:
Great Compassion Mantra Eliminates Accidents

True benefits are often difficult to express.

Like a person drinking water,

only you know if it's cold or hot.

Even when the weather is extremely hot, you are not afraid of the heat or the long distance to the high mountains. Is there any benefit to coming here to participate in a meditation retreat? True benefit is often difficult to express. Just like a person drinking water, whether it's cold or hot only knows for himself. Only people with a true mind can comprehend the miracle.

How to reap this benefit? Nothing more than sincerely reciting the Bodhisattva's name. Sincerity means being single-minded. So it is said: "If you specialize, you will be flexible, if you divide, you will be bad." That is, if you specialize, you will be flexible, if you divide, you will be deadlocked. When the mind is single, the path will naturally be felt. The induction of communication is inherently inconceivable. However, you have to work hard yourself, other people can't do it for you, and you can't even pray for luck.

Just like " talks about eating rice or counting money for others." Some people often mention nutritious things like this and that, but they don't eat them themselves, so no matter how nutritious the food is, they can't enjoy it. So say:

Share the daily book and forgive the treasure, sell the money yourself.

If you don't practice the dharma, it's strange that the heron is like this.

Mean:

Counting people's money all day long, not a penny myself.

Studying the Dharma without practicing, the same mistakes are made.

I recite Buddha's name the same way. It is not enough to understand or discuss the merits of reciting the Bodhisattva; You must really recite until your mind is undisturbed; Even when the water flows and the wind blows, our ears only hear the sound of the Bodhisattva's name. So say:

Intentionally, unintentionally,

Ensemble performance of Maha-dharma.

Meaning:

Sentient or inanimate species,

All talk about the wonderful dharma of Mahayana.

If we cannot recite to the point of undivided attention, then even if the wind blows and the water gurgles, we will not be able to feel its magic. Therefore, we must be sincere in our thoughts and not be enticed by false thoughts in order to reap the benefits of the Dharma.

When entering a room, you must respect the rules of the room. Because "No rules any rules can become a party." That is, without rules, it cannot become a party. Tay Lac Vien's rule is not to speak loudly to avoid hindering others from practicing.

During these seven days, we also recite the Great Compassion Mantra. The merits of the Great Compassion Mantra are very difficult to imagine. If people do not have good roots, it will be difficult for them to hear the three words "Great Compassion Mantra." Now the masses have not only heard but also Receiving and Upholding the chant, enough to know that you have full good roots. If you already have good roots, you should not underestimate it and do not let this life pass by in vain.

I still remember when Tay Lac Vien Pagoda passed away for the first time, out of ten Lay Buddhists, eight or nine of them could not recite the Great Compassion Mantra. But now, out of ten people, eight can recite it. This proves the progress of the Lay Buddhists. I tell you a story to demonstrate the merits of Uncle Dai-Bi.

Manchuria had a tycoon who bought a lot of real estate. One fall, this tycoon himself took four or five carts full of sorghum to the street to sell. Because it was more than 150 miles from the countryside to the city, he departed at 1:00 a.m. Unfortunately, half way there, I encountered a robber. Seeing this, he immediately recited the Great Compassion Mantra. Strange! The bandits were blind and could not see his car, so he safely escaped danger. That was one of the inspirations of the Great Compassion Mantra that I personally witnessed.

The Great Compassion Dharani Sutra teaches that: "Whoever recites the Great Compassion Mantra can eliminate avoid disasters: Fire cannot burn, water cannot drown." Therefore, I advise you to recite it at least three times a day. If you don't know how to recite, then learn quickly. The merit of reciting the Great Compassion Mantra can not only repel thieves and robbers, but also eliminate hundreds of diseases and escape the harassment of demons. Therefore, you should sincerely recite it.

Today is the first day of the retreat, the atmosphere of the Dharma conference is very excited and serious. I hope you will make an effort and be diligent.

Lunch lecture on June 13, 1958 in Tay Lac Vien, Hong Kong

Just make diligent efforts,

then I can "Return."

Errors that were not fixed in the past but are now understood.

The above poem was composed by Mr. Ngu Lieu (Dao Uyen Minh). But I wonder if the poet really understands the profound meaning of the poem's words? Because if we look at Buddha's teachings, the above poem makes perfect sense.

Why is it called "Back to the past?" We know that the Dharmakaya's self-nature is the permanent place of light of the Buddhas of the ten directions. The sutra writes: "All Sentient Beings have Buddha nature." My nature and that of Buddha are inherently no different. If it weren't like that, how could it be said that "all have Buddha nature." Now we cannot realize Buddha nature because we are polluted by the world's five desires of the Ta-ba world. Because we are not fully aware of the world, we cannot understand our own mind and cannot fully see our original nature.

However, we cannot go crazy forever. We must return to our original form and return to the world of enlightenment. That is "Return to the past." It means we have to restore our original appearance. When we rely on the power of Buddha Bodhisattva's vows, thanks to the merit of chanting His holy name, we are born in the Pure Land. That is also called "Past."

Once we have realized our own mind and been born in the Pure Land, we need to make a great vow: "Reversing the price from goods," means driving the boat of compassion back to help Sentient Beings to the shore of peace. That's called "hybrid," which means Return.

What is " Dien Vien Tuong Vu Ho Irregular?" Dien means field, is the field of mind. When we do not cultivate our mind and let random thoughts arise, it is like a field full of weeds. The field of mind becomes wild. "Impossible knots opening," If weeds abound, if we can't pull them out, then we have no way to return to our original nature and clear our minds to realize our nature.

"The Lake of Irregularity" are the words of the Buddhas of the ten directions and the Saints. They kindly teach us that: "Sentient Beings are so stupid and pitiful! Why don't you guys quickly turn around and return to the wharf?"

"The mind is in a state of translation" means that the mind is controlled by the body and it means that Sentient Beings, because of their attachment to the six senses, cannot realize their own mind, are always controlled by the world, so they are busy with life, for fame and profit regardless of life, moving in the sea of suffering of birth and death, experiencing countless sufferings. It is truly a thousand years of sadness and suffering that cannot be fully expressed. That is the meaning of the sentence "Trù swollen like poison."

So, do Sentient Beings have no cure? Is it true that I will forever fall into the abyss of the six paths of reincarnation? Absolutely not. Even though I made mistakes in the past, looking to the future there is still hope. You should know that "The future is only traceable, " knows that the future can still catch up and can still be saved.

In the future, we should not be like the past, abandoning enlightenment, following the dust of the world, making our mind a slave to our body. In the past, I didn't believe in Cause and Effect, not practicing diligently, creating karma, killing, etc. were all wrong things. Like today, reciting the Buddha's name is the right thing to do. So we "Golden Horn thi Nhi tat phi," means "Understand what was right today, yesterday was wrong." For good deeds, we must maintain, for bad deeds, we must immediately wholeheartedly repent. The ancients said: "The most light and sound, the most gold." That means one inch of time is one inch of gold. Actually, for practitioners, a period of time is a period of life. As time passes, my life becomes a little shorter.

As today passes, the network will also decrease;

The masses! Be diligent and diligent like saving your head.

We must quickly correct evil and do good. Because I'm "I'm really into things very strange," that means I haven't gone deep into the dark path yet. The World of Ultimate Bliss is right in front of our eyes. As long as we make diligent efforts, we can "Go back to the past."

tieu_de: Repentance means Self-Reformation
tom_tat: Buddha's dharma power is very great, but the karma power of Sentient Beings is also very great, so there is a saying: "Ordinary people's karma is heavy and passionate, Buddha's karma is devoted and empty." Therefore, the difference between saints and mortals is that "karma" has...
noi_dung:
Repentance means Self-Reformation

If you truly have the heart to repent, then why are you afraid that there is no hope?

The Buddha's dharma power is very great, but the karma of Sentient Beings is also very great, so there is a saying: "Ordinary people have heavy karma of passion, Buddha's karma is not devoted." Therefore, the difference between saints and mortals is whether "karma" has ended, and whether there is still "love" or not.

Enlightenment, Buddha,

Sentient Beings.

Meaning:

When enlightenment is Buddha,

when in delusion, it is Sentient Beings.

Sentient Beings are incompatible with the world (turning away from enlightenment and wisdom to mingle with the dust of ignorance), always being turned around by the world of the five desires (greed for wealth, greed for beauty, greed for fame, greed for food, greed for sleep), causing karma to increase day by day. Buddha transcends all five worldly desires and no longer creates karma. Sentient Beings, due to their heavy karma, want to attain enlightenment and become Buddhas, they must first repent of the sins they have committed. If you don't have the heart to repent and want to become a Buddha, it's like cooking sand and hoping it becomes rice. Even though sand has been cooked for countless eons, in the end it cannot become rice. "Repentance" means to repent of past mistakes, to be ashamed of mistakes made. "Repent" is to repent or amend; I am determined to change my personality and never repeat the same mistake again. As Mr. Vien Lieu Pham said:

Of pre-existing species, such as carving a sunflower.

The origin of the race is like the birthday diamond.

Meaning:

Bad things I did before,

yesterday was like the last day.

Things I will do later,

today is the start of a new life.

If we do not repent diligently, the karma we create will cause us to fall forever. Surely you remember that when taking refuge, you first confess your name and then repent as follows:

Tung u has no beginning, only gold is born,

Canceling the Three Jewels, creating Icchantika,

The Mahayana Sutra, the passage on Prajnaparamita,

Harming parents, giving birth to Buddha's body and blood,

The monks are greedy, destroy the virtuous conduct, destroy the pagoda, use the teachings of the monks, give rise to wrong views, reject the cause and effect, be close to the evil friends, be a good teacher...

Meaning:

From beginningless time, until today,

Curse the Three Jewels, do Icchantika,

Curse the Mahayana Sutra, stop studying Prajnaparamita,

Killed mother and father, shed Buddha's blood,

Dirty in temples, destroying people's morality Burning pagodas and towers, stealing monks' belongings, raising all kinds of wrong ideas, saying no Cause and Effect

Close to bad friends, go against good teachers...

Now, I will re-explain the general idea of the above repentance passage.

From beginningless time until now, we have created countless karma, unspeakable. First, we blaspheme the Three Jewels: Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha. Among the crimes, slandering "Monks-treasure" is the biggest and heaviest sin, because the Sangha represents Buddha to promote Buddha-Dharma. Therefore, defaming the Sangha is a sin that cannot be repented. What is called "Exhibit"? "Xianti" in Sanskrit translates to "not having good faith,"not having enough faith, or "not having good roots,"not having good roots. For example, when you preach the Dharma to that person, not only do they not like to listen, but they even say the opposite: "I don't believe it!" Isn't this cutting off your own good roots?

"Slandering the Mahayana Sutras" means defaming the Mahayana Sutras. For example, some people say that the principles in the sutras are false or say that the Mahayana sutras were spoken by the devil, etc. This is also a sin that cannot be repented. "Prajna" is Sanskrit, meaning wisdom. There are three types of Prajna: Real Form Prajna, Prajna of Contemplation and Prajna of Literature. If "learns" (refuses to learn) any kind of Prajna, then we will become foolish. The retribution of foolishness is to fall into the state of an animal.

"Killing one's parents" means killing one's parents. This verse also includes the killing of Arahants and saints. For example, Devadatta killed a person who attained the Four Arahants.

Next is "Exciting the Buddha's body and blood" which means raising the Buddha's blood. This is also a sin that cannot be repented of. Many people misunderstand that this crime only applies when the Buddha is still alive. When you use a knife to cut and slash the Buddha's body, you will incur this crime. But really, after the Buddha passed away, whenever we destroy Buddha statues or Buddha images, we all commit this crime. Breaking the gold layer on the Buddha statue or smashing the Buddha statue, although it does not harm the Buddha's flesh, is still cutting and cutting the Buddha's body.

"O monk lam" means to pollute the pure place of the temple. Like some Lay Buddhists whose families reside in the temple, but do unjust things such as eating meat, killing animals, etc. "Destroying the holy conduct" means destroying the pure conduct of others. For example, monastics have always been pure and undefiled, but some people harass them, causing them to break the precepts, which is also a sin that cannot be repented.

"The part of destroying temple towers" means burning or destroying or destroying temple towers and pagodas. For example, in history, Phung Ngoc Tuong burned the Pagoda

White Horse and Shaolin Temple. "The practice of using monks" is to steal monks' belongings. This refers to those who use unjust means to take permanent property as their own. Such people all have wrong knowledge, wrong views, wrong ideas, and always think they are right. They often believe that there is no Cause and Effect and always do things that go against morality. There is no evil or bad thing that they do not dare to do. How can such a person not fall into hell?

Finally, "Associating with evil friends, great elders and teachers" means being close to evil people, bad friends and opposing good teachers. Bad friends are those whom Confucian scholars call "harmful friends" (harming friends). Robbers and dishonest people who live outside the law are things you should not make friends with. Associating with them will only harm you, slowly making you go down the wrong path, no longer listening to the advice of your parents and good teachers; taking what is wrong as right and no longer being able to distinguish between right and wrong, black and white, just doing things arrogantly, how pitiful!

The above sins are things that we should not commit, even though they are very easy to commit. What should I do if I accidentally make those mistakes? Don't be afraid. There is a saying: "Heavenly commits a great sin, repentance is easily eliminated." Meaning, the crime is astronomical, repentance is completely eliminated. Sin has no form. If we truly have the heart to repent, then there is no fear that there is no hope. You should not look down on yourself, do not be willing to fall into ruin.

Lecture on June 14, 1958

tieu_de: Inciting Others to Do Evil, Your Crime Is Tripled
tom_tat: No matter who we ask for repentance in front of, we must express our mistakes clearly and must not say vague or ambiguous words.
noi_dung:
Inciting Others to Do Evil, Your Crime Triples

No matter who we ask for repentance in front of, we must express our mistakes clearly and not say vague or insinuating words.

Yesterday I gave you a simple lecture on the meaning of repentance, only teaching up to the paragraph "Being close to evil friends, ruining ancestors and teachers." Now I will continue to explain the following paragraph:

"Self-teaching tha" means doing it yourself, inciting others to do it, or seeing or hearing others do it, and agreeing to do it. We must know that killing, stealing, adultery, lying or drinking are all unjust actions, which create karma. These crimes are divided into four categories:

Causes, conditions, dharma, karma (causes, supporting conditions, methods and actions). Killing includes killing people, killing conditions, killing dharma, and killing karma; Regardless of which precepts, there is "self-action" or "teaching others, " means doing it yourself or inciting others to do it.

"Do it yourself" means not using the hands of others, but doing the illegal thing yourself. "Inciting someone else to do" means telling someone else to do something that is not right. That is an indirect crime. Compared to direct sin, this indirect sin is a bit more serious, because we are already guilty of sin, but we also carry the additional sin of deceit. So doing it yourself is of course a sin, but inciting others to do it is an even more serious sin.

What is "joyful writing"? (seeing, hearing, then rejoicing), which means that we know that someone else has committed a crime but we also help that person, just like the ancients said: "Supporting Tru Vi Xuyet" means helping King Tru do tyrannical things. Try closing your eyes and imagine that from beginningless time until now, how many times have you made this mistake? There's no need to think back that far. Just considering this short life, the crimes I committed are already unspeakable.

Therefore, in the next Repentance article is the sentence: "Such sins are equal, immeasurable and boundless." Meaning that such sins have no bounds and cannot be limited. Not only are my sins impossible to enumerate, but they are also infinitely numerous. If I already know that my sin is so deep, what should I do now? Without saying anything, I know that I need to urgently repent before Buddha.

That's why the Repentance article continues: "The old man is born in a golden day, giving birth to great treasures. Carved into skin, asking someone to repent." "Carved into" These two words mean sincerity. When repenting, the most important thing is to be sincere. There are people who repent to their master, but they are extremely deceitful. But usually they keep their heads and tails hidden. Disguise and hide their sins. That is also a sign that they do not sincerely repent of their sins. With such a cunning way of repenting, even if they go through hundreds of millions of millions of lives, countless eons, it will be impossible for their sins to be completely eliminated.

Therefore, saying "The upright mind is Bodhimanda" means that the upright mind is Bodhimanda. When repenting to someone, we must express our mistakes clearly, and must not say words with ambiguous or double meanings. For example, when asking if there is any crime? Then answer that "I don't remember" or "maybe" etc. Such incomplete repentance not only fails to eliminate karma but also plants more bad karma. In Buddhism, even something as small as a hair must not be careless or taken lightly. But someone gave the following example: "There is a man who always creates bad things, does evil things, but for some reason he is still doing rich business right now, so there is no Cause and Effect, no justice, right?" There is a verse as follows:

Despite the hardships of hundreds of thousands of kalpas, the work will not perish; When the fate meets, the retribution is fulfilled.

Meaning:

After hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, the karma created does not disappear; When the time is right, the karma will be rewarded.

Therefore, we must know that the karma we create will have its consequences; It's just a matter of time, whether it's fast or slow, and whether the fates have fully come together yet.

Some people say that if "After hundreds of thousands of lifetimes, the karma created does not disappear, then is there no way for us to eliminate our sins?" It is not that there is no solution. The method to eliminate karma is "Only praying for the Three Jewels, compassionately taking in life, releasing pure light, illuminating the body." Meaning praying for the Three Jewels, compassionately guiding, releasing good light, illuminating your body. I hope that the Buddha, Dharma, Sangha, and Three Jewels can follow their compassionate wishes and use pure, unobstructed light to illuminate their bodies. When the light shines on your body, the three obstacles (obstacles of afflictions, obstacles of retribution, and obstacles of karma) are eliminated. Just like the drifting clouds and moon appear, the pure original nature of your mind emerges again. Therefore, it is said "All evils are destroyed, and the three obstacles are eliminated. Restoring the original mind, the goal is pure." Meaning that after the evil is destroyed, the three hindrances will be swept away. Restore the source of the eternally pure mind.

After finishing preaching this article on Repentance, I hope that you will understand the harm of not repenting and the benefits of repentance. There is also a repentance article as follows:

Remaining behind creates evil karma,

Due to beginningless greed, anger and ignorance,

The birthplace of body, speech, and mind,

Absolutely fall into the golden stage of repentance.

Translated as:

All evil karma created in the past,

It's all due to beginningless greed, anger, and ignorance,

was born from body, mouth, and mind. I now repent for everything.

This repentance article can not only make you repent of your sins, but also show the cause of committing sins. Therefore, I hope that you will recite this text at least three times every day in front of the Buddha table. Now I will briefly explain the meaning of this article to you.

"Remnant" means in the past; Near means in this life, but far away means countless lifetimes ago. During that time, not only was I born into the womb of a buffalo or born into a horse, I was also born into the Truong family, and sometimes became a child of the Ly family. Circulating in the six paths, and during this period, I don't know how much karma I have created.

Why do I create pity? The repentance article explains very clearly, "It's all due to beginningless greed, anger, and ignorance" meaning that due to the three poisons of greed, anger, and ignorance, countless karmas arise. Also because of these three poisons, our bodies commit crimes such as killing, stealing, and lust. The mouth gives rise to the sins of lying, lying, saying evil things, and using double tongues. Therefore, in the article it is said that " is born from the body, speech, and mind." means that it arises from the body, speech, and mind.

Regardless of whether the sin is committed by the body such as killing, stealing, or lust, or by the mouth, such as lying, speaking evil words, embellishing words, using a double tongue, or by sin arising from the mind such as greed, anger, and ignorance, we must urgently repent. Otherwise, we are like someone falling into the mud, sinking deeper and deeper. When our sins become more and more serious, we have nowhere to go, and there is no way to save ourselves.

I hope that all of you sitting here now have good roots, do not forget about repentance, you can definitely make a vow to repent of your karma and eliminate all sins.

Lecture June 15, 1958

tieu_de: Cultivation Has Four Stages
tom_tat: There are four seasons in a year: Spring, summer, autumn, winter. That's obvious, everyone knows. But did you know that human life is also divided into four stages: Birth, old age, illness, and death. As a human, everyone dies, so we have to figure out...
noi_dung:
Practice Has Four Stages

Consider the day of refuge as a birthday.

The life of practice starts from there.

There are four seasons in a year: Spring, summer, autumn, winter. That's obvious, everyone knows. But did you know that human life is also divided into four stages: Birth, old age, illness, and death. As a human, everyone dies, so we have to think about the future and cultivate the Way. Cultivation also has four stages, i.e. learning, practice, accomplishment, and completion.

From the moment of birth to the age of twenty, a human being is a period of learning the Way. During this period, we must learn and study Buddhism well. Just like in the book The University, it is said: "Because of clear intelligence." It means to shine the virtue of insight. That's when we train our virtues to become more and more pure. From the age of twenty-one until forty is the period of practicing the Dharma. This is the time to apply what you have learned; bring your previous learning and understanding to the spectrum of Sentient Beings, the secular world. As in the book University-University it is written: "For the sake of the people" means to renew people's lives. From the age of forty-one to the age of sixty is called the time of attaining the Tao. In the book The University, it is written: "Only good intentions" means stopping at the best place. Confucius preached "goodwill" but not very thoroughly, because he had not yet reached the realm of True Emptiness Nirvana, so it was not the ultimate goal. Therefore, at the final stage, we need to " attain the Way." After achieving the Way, we return to the realm of Nirvana. If compared with the three credos of Confucianism: "Mighty-virtue, friendly-people, only-goodness", the Buddhist principles of practice are much more comprehensive.

Someone said: "From the time I was little until I was twenty years old, I did not believe in Buddha. Now, when it comes to studying the Way, that time has passed. How can I still learn? Do I not need to study?" You must understand, when I talk about the four stages, it is only an ideal, not a fixed, immutable thing. Therefore, we can consider the day of refuge as a birthday, and then from that day count it as the time to start practicing.

Some people say: "I've been taking refuge for four years, but why haven't I learned a bit of Buddhism?" Actually, even though you've taken refuge for four or five years, to Buddhism, you're just a four or five year old child. Therefore, don't worry about not being able to do anything. Buddha-dharma is very profound. As long as after I take refuge, I make twenty years of effort to study the Way, twenty years of effort to practice it, then will I not have a day of accomplishment?

all working haphazardly,

not knowing how to take care of the body.

Tu Hau Phuong Tri uses his mind.

But by the time I knew that, it was too late. Should say:

Lam Nhai Lac Ma Thu Cuong Tuong.

The boat begins to expand the mind to replenish the emptiness!

The horse reaches the abyss, it's too late to take the reins.

The boat reached the middle of the stream, patching the hole was very slow!

That's why Chu Tu said it very well: "Nghi vo er tru tru mau, vo lam thich er quach static." Meaning when it hasn't rained yet, we have to make arrangements in advance; For example, repairing the roof. When it hasn't rained yet, we have to quickly prepare for what will happen when it rains. Immortals elaborate.

tieu_de: Reciting the Bodhisattva's Name can clear the mind and see nature
tom_tat: The nature of Sentient Beings is to like happiness and hate suffering. Due to ignorance, Sentient Beings do not know how to achieve peace and happiness, to escape suffering. Therefore, although the mouth always says that it is the pursuit of peace...
noi_dung:
Reciting the Bodhisattva's Name can enlighten the mind and see nature

The nature of Sentient Beings, always bright and brilliant.

It's just because it's obscured by countless sins and false thoughts.

The nature of Sentient Beings is to like happiness and hate suffering. Due to ignorance, Sentient Beings do not know how to achieve peace and happiness, to escape suffering. Therefore, although we always say we are pursuing peace, unfortunately, the more we search, the more painful we become.

A Bodhisattva is a person who has great compassion, is enlightened, and knows how to leave suffering and attain happiness. Therefore, towards the suffering and pitiable Sentient Beings, He made a great and compassionate wish to save suffering. So Sentient Beings themselves are not completely hopeless. As long as we have a sincere heart and chant "Namo Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva,", He will use boundless dharma power to save us, help us escape suffering, and attain happiness. This peace is the final peace, the peace in the Western Pure Land. Therefore, it is said that by reciting the Bodhisattva's name, not only can we escape the suffering of this world, but we can also be reborn in the world of Ultimate Bliss, when flowers open our eyes to see Buddha, and we can reach the ultimate peaceful, pure place.

Reciting the Bodhisattva's name can let go of suffering and make you realize your mind's nature. Is there such a thing as being so easy? Many Sentient Beings are still ignorant, asking this question. The Bodhisattva was determined to make things convenient for Sentient Beings, so he introduced such a method of expediency. However, there are still many Sentient Beings who, even with that ultimate ease, are not aware of it. What a pity!

Some people say: "Reciting the Bodhisattva's name can eliminate sins and suffering, that's what I believe. But how can reciting the Bodhisattva's name make me clear my mind and realize my nature?" A few days ago, I gave the example of typing on the phone. Now, let me tell you another even simpler example.

For example, there is a person who is blindfolded and sees only four dark pools. Wherever that person goes, if he doesn't bump into the wall, he will bump into the wall, causing his head to break and his forehead to break, causing him to be unable to speak. But, he didn't know how to remove the mask. Fortunately, he met a compassionate person who saw him so pitifully and helped him remove the blindfold. Thanks to that, from not being able to see the road, he can now see everything, no longer suffering, nor having to walk and bump into walls like before.

The principle of reciting the Bodhisattva's name to gain insight into one's nature is similar. Sentient Beings, just like that blindfolded person, their eyes are not blind, they are just covered. The mentality of Sentient Beings is the same, never lost, always bright and brilliant. It's just because it's obscured by countless sins and false thoughts. Bodhisattva is like that compassionate person. He helps us eliminate the karma that has covered up the luminous nature in our hearts; so that I can return to my original duties and return to my original position; Restore original item appearance.

Therefore, we cannot help but chant the Bodhisattva's name. Because, like that blindfolded person, if you don't ask others, refuse to accept help from others, not only will you still have to bump into the wall, but you can also go astray and fall into an abyss, endangering your life.

In this world, the number of people who commit crimes is countless. If you are not careful, if you lose your step one day, fall into the abyss of sin, and lose your human body, it will be difficult for you to find it again for thousands of lifetimes, and you will hold a grudge for thousands of years. Lay Buddhists! Quickly accept the advice of the Bodhisattva and regularly chant His name to be saved from this sea of ​​suffering of birth and death.

Concentration is very important for practitioners; Without concentration, cultivating the path will naturally fail. Without the power of concentration, the spiritual mind is not solid and can easily be influenced by outside influences, causing one to fall.

Next is Hue, which means wisdom. As humans, there are smart people and stupid people. Why are some people smart and some people stupid? This is due to Cause and Effect. If you practiced reciting the Buddha's name in the past, you will definitely have wisdom in this life; On the contrary, without cultivating good roots, wisdom naturally does not exist.

There is Peace and then Morning,

It's OK to Have Morning.

Therefore, only with Concentration can Hue be born. If there is no Concentration, full of random thoughts, and wandering thoughts, how can we see right and wrong clearly, and the truth clearly?

Precepts are rules that help us prevent committing crimes. When you have not committed a crime, you need to practice the Way. The secret to cultivating the Way is concentration. Having the power of concentration gives rise to wisdom, from which one can attain Buddhahood. So Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom are indispensable conditions that people who practice the Way must have. If you don't keep the precepts, you can create bad karma. If you lack concentration, you won't be able to practice the Way. If you don't have wisdom, you'll be foolish.

I advise you to take "Precepts and Concentration Hue" these three words deeply engraved in your heart, and often bring them to your attention. I believe that for practice, they are very helpful.

Lecture June 18, 1958

tieu_de: Water Flowing In Front Of The Temple Door
tom_tat: Today is the Bodhisattva's feast day. Although Tay Lac Vien Pagoda (Hong Kong) is built on a remote mountain, you have to climb three hundred steps to reach it; But when you come here to participate in the retreat, you will be extremely happy, enough to see that you have the heart...
noi_dung:
Flowing Water In Front Of The Temple

This side has never had water but suddenly there is.

Is this really what I brought about?

Today is the Bodhisattva's feast day. Although Tay Lac Vien Pagoda (Hong Kong) is built on a remote mountain, you have to climb three hundred steps to reach it; But when you come here to participate in the retreat, you will be extremely happy, enough to see that you have a sincere heart and a spirit of bravery and diligence.

In terms of the number of people participating in the retreat, each year there are more and more people. Many people here, after returning from bowing to Buddha, said that their business was more favorable than before.

Like Lay Buddhist Vien Qua Lam, from the day he arrived at the temple, his work became more and more prosperous. As for Lay Buddhist Dam Qua Boc, since the day he took refuge, his blessings and longevity have increased. This year, at the age of eighty, his body is extremely strong.

There was a child who was crippled from four to nine years old and could not walk, but when he came here to worship Buddha, his leg was healed and he could walk and stand. The daughter of the Vien Chan family was also sick. She sought Chinese medicine and took Western medicine, but her illness did not heal. After bowing to Buddha, her illness was cured immediately. That's why many people propagate that I can cure illnesses, but it's really just because of the merit of bowing to Buddha.

There is another thing worth calling a memory: Before Tay Lac Vien Pagoda was established, this land was a hole seven or eight meters deep. After that, the workers poured land and leveled it to make the pagoda. This land has never had water, but after Bodhimanda was built, there was an endless source of water flowing out. Some people say that I brought this water from Phu Dung mountain. Because when I was at Phu Dung mountain, Avalokitesvara cave, there was water outside the cave, but strangely when I arrived at this temple, the water on the other side had dried up. This side has never had water, but suddenly there is. Is this really what I brought about? That is definitely due to Buddha's inspiration and Thien Long's support.

Today you are so happy and enthusiastic, but the fun quickly ends and you have to wait until next year to practice another course. Next year, if you want to participate in Avalokitesvara, you must register early and make a vow to complete the meditation. In November, there will be Amitabha That. You need to be brave and diligent in participating without being lazy or lazy.

Now I have the unsurpassed Dharma method to tell you, but before I tell you the Dharma, you must know that seeking the Dharma is not easy. Therefore, you must comply with my words that after listening, you must follow the Dharma and practice before I can tell you.

In this method, you must make a vow every day in front of the Buddha:

Sentient Beings have boundless vows of salvation.

Endless sorrow and broken vows.

There are countless Dharma teachings to vow to learn.

Buddha's supreme vow is fulfilled.

You all clearly understand these four great vows. All Buddhas attained enlightenment from these four vows. Bodhisattvas also practice from this place of prayer. There are also a few prayers that you are more knowledgeable about, that is:

I wish to be born in the Western Pure Land,

Nine Chapters are lotus flowers for parents.

Flowers opened Buddha's eyes to enlightenment without birth.

Unrelenting Bodhisattva is a traveling companion.

If you can make such a vow every day, I am confident that you will meet the Buddha, will not retreat on the path of learning the Way, and will soon become Buddha.

Lecture June 19, 1958

tieu_de: Gia Phong of Kim Son Thanh Tu
tom_tat: Waking up at two o'clock in the morning and meditating until midnight before falling asleep. There was only one break during the whole session
noi_dung:
Gia Phong of Kim Son Thanh Tu

Wake up at two o'clock in the morning and meditate until midnight before falling asleep. There was only one hour of rest during the whole day.

Golden Feng for nine days, seven years, six years, the assembly of the Ten Directions again meditated. At the moment of division of meditation, the act of sitting is supported by all meditation. Emptiness has destroyed the mind and earth, the Dharma-world has naturally seen the nature of heaven. In the future, I face the mist and rivers of the land, Directly down to the Yang Mountain Temple.

Meaning:

Today is the year one nine seven six,

The masses of the ten directions return to meditate.

The ticking moments need to be treasured,

Walking, standing, lying down, and sharpening.

Smash the void at the heart of the light,

Yet the Dharma-realm sees the natural nature.

Where to find the original item?

Right here, right away: Kim Son Tu.

Today is the full moon day of December 1976. Those of you with good roots in the ten directions come to the furnace of Kim Son Thanh Temple to meditate. Meditation is no joke, it entails much suffering. In the morning, I start waking up at two o'clock to meditate (incense sitting). Sitting continuously until 12 o'clock at night before falling asleep, in between only having an hour to rest. This is the family tradition of Kim Son Thanh Tu.

During the period of meditation, we must forget our body, our mind, and the whole world; everything is forgotten; That is, there is no longer "self", which also means everything is empty. When you reach such a realm of emptiness, you will be born with wonderful existence. You must pay attention! While practicing, we cannot talk arbitrarily, rest arbitrarily, cannot have false thoughts, nor can we be lazy or try to go to sleep. Every hour, every minute, every second must be cherished and regretted, so people say:

The light of the day, the light of destiny.

Meaning:

A little time is a little life.

Therefore, when walking, also meditate, when standing, also meditate, when sitting, also meditate, and when lying down, also meditate. Walking, standing, lying down, and sitting are all meditation. It should be said that you need to skillfully hone your mind. Sharpen and sharpen, the more you sharpen, the clearer you become.

Honing is the first conversation, don't stop, don't stop. Always refer to the question "Who is Buddha's name?" or refer to the question "When our parents had not yet given birth to us, what did our face look like?" Therefore, it should be said that we need to grind and grind until one day we will "smash the nothingness" (referring to ignorance). At that time, we will clearly understand our mind. Even though the void has been destroyed by us, the Dharma-world still exists. That dharma-realm, that is, the ten dharma-realms, still exists, without any chaos at all. That's when I saw my natural nature. Where should you find your original face? You should go to Kim Son Thanh Tu to find your original appearance. You go somewhere else and are afraid you won't find it anywhere.

The eight verses I said today, I hope you will pay attention to them and practice according to them. You cannot eat without digesting them, that is truly absurd. Don't consider this as the wind blowing through your ears. Having heard it is the same as not having heard it yet, it is of no benefit at all.

Lecture on December 15, 1976 on the occasion of Zen retreat at Kim Son Thanh Tu

tieu_de: Studying Buddhism requires a sincere heart
tom_tat: To study Buddha-Dharma, you need to have a sincere mind, every move, every word, every action must be true. Don't be like worldly people, half true and half false. When speaking, sometimes there is a bit of honesty; sometimes full of lies. Cultivators…
noi_dung:
Learning Buddhism requires a sincere heart

Every move, every word, every behavior, must all be truthful.

To study Buddha-Dharma, you need to have a sincere mind, every move, every word, every action must be true. Don't be like worldly people, half true and half false. When speaking, sometimes there is a bit of honesty; sometimes full of lies. People who practice the Way must always speak the truth, do the truth, and must not lie. For every concept, mistakes must be eliminated; Eliminate the habit of countless lifetimes and try to change it. The sins we have committed in countless lifetimes must be repented of completely.

Why are there people who have studied Buddhism for so many years without any correspondence at all? It's because we still cover up our mistakes and refuse to practice with our true mind. So time passes in vain without realizing true wisdom, and also without true concentration. Time passes unjustly, but our karma is not achieved, which is a pity.

Living in a temple, we need to be frugal with all material things. There is a saying:

Desire for permanent objects,

Like the label of Central Asia.

Meaning:

Take advantage of the temple's treasures,

Like preserving the pupil (in the eye).

Temple items such as rice, oil, soy sauce or vinegar, we must cherish them and not waste them carelessly. Even the things we use, a blade of grass, a piece of wood, a page of paper, we must know how to value and be thrifty. If we are not careful in these places and do not know how to be grateful for our blessings, how much merit will we waste? That:

Cultivation, not like creation,

What you get, no matter where you are.

Meaning:

The effort we put into cultivating is not equal to the karma we create. What we gain is less than what we lose.

One more thing is that with every action, every word, and every conduct, you must not harm others. When speaking, you must use virtuous words; Do not speak slander (fabricated words), lies, evil words or double words. The mouth is something that we need to pay special attention to. The body is not allowed to kill, not to steal, not to commit adultery. The mind should not commit greed, anger and ignorance, and should not take this stinky flesh and skin seriously. If your mind thinks that you secretly steal food for this body, look for clothes and jewelry, or find ways for this body to enjoy and be happy, then that is all crazy! We have to think about how to leave the three realms (Desire Realm, Form Realm, Formless Realm), escape from the six paths (hell, hungry ghosts, animals, Asuras, humans and gods) in this cycle of reincarnation, and how to change our habits. Must empty the tank of love. Only then will I be satisfied with achieving Bodhi.

"If you practice the religion, you will not receive blessings." Remember the example of the Elders of Buddhism. Buddha Shakyamuni was the most noble prince, but he was able to give up everything to become a monk and practice the Way. If we talk about status, even though he has become a monk, he can still eat well and dress well, and live in a nice and luxurious temple; but He did not do that. He went to Tuyet Son mountain and endured suffering, hunger, thirst, heat and cold, and practiced for six years. During those six years, he did not eat delicious food, did not stay in a beautiful place, and did not call people to make offerings. He just stayed there enduring all the hardships.

Try to think about the noble status of Shakyamuni Buddha, who willingly endured such suffering and practice; Then try to think about your fate? I am just an ordinary person, so why do I want to eat well, wear nice clothes, live in a good place, be greedy for enjoyment, not endure hardship and still fear suffering! Think about it, if you compare yourself with Shakyamuni Buddha, wouldn't you be extremely ashamed?

You have to act like you didn't do anything.

When you finish something, don't accept it

before what merit is there.

The act of non-dwelling and rebirth.

Extremely endless meaning of divination.

The Tathagata of the ten directions receive the same blessing.

Let go of suffering and gain happiness.

Meaning:

If you don't bow and bow, you will be reborn.

Rich meaning without end.

The Tathagata of the ten directions received the same blessing.

Escape the pit of suffering and find happiness.

Buddhism often has the saying: "If you want to have no place to live, you will give birth to the mind" (start the mind without dwelling on any concept, emotion or appearance at all). Therefore, when teaching the Shurangama Mantra, I said: "The ritual does not exist, transforms and is reborn." This word "sanh" means endless birth, endless transformation. The ceremony is to bow to the Buddhas. Non-attachment means no attachment. You say: "If I don't practice anything, I won't have any attachments!" That's wrong! When practicing, you should not be attached to the fact that you practice. You say: "If I don't have an attachment to not eating or drinking when I'm not eating or drinking, then my stomach won't agree." However, if you're full and want to eat more, that's not right. The Diamond Sutra says: "Start thinking but don't focus on anything."

Today there is a person who thinks that the sentence "Starts the mind but does not dwell on anything " thinks that there is no need to practice, no need to recite mantras, and no need to chant sutras; Only then will you not be attached. That's not true! I have to "do it without incident" - do it as if I didn't do it at all. When you do something, you should not be attached to the idea that you have this or that merit, that is baseless. When there is a place to stand in front of, there is a place of attachment, a place of stuckness, where escape is impossible. Therefore, in the depths of your mind, don't dwell on anything, wipe out all dharmas, stay away from all appearances. At that time, the birth and transformation (the scene manifested by the true mind) will be endless. Therefore, the sentence: "Infinite meaning di style" is saying the infinity of the meaning of the Shurangama Mantra. The meaning of the Mantra is so numerous that there is nothing more to it.

Because of that, when I recite a Shurangama Mantra, "The Tathagata of the ten directions receive their blessings, " The Buddhas of the ten directions all receive their blessings, just like when I treat a baby: "My child, don't cry anymore! Here I give you candy. Stop crying! Wait a minute, I'll give you an apple!" When the baby hears an apple, its ears perk up, paying attention. tieu_de: When the heart has lustful thoughts, it is like wealth
tom_tat: All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, saints, and monks all have immeasurable wisdom and light. That wisdom is the wisdom that has no outflows or no outflows
noi_dung:
When there is desire in the heart, it is like wealth

taken by robbers.

All Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, saints, and monks all have immeasurable wisdom and light. That wisdom is boundless wisdom.

Every ordinary person is a degenerate because of ignorance. Buddhas and Bodhisattvas are anasrava because they are no longer ignorant. Ignorance means not understanding, being confused, not knowing what is right and what is wrong, not being able to distinguish white from black.

The biggest defilement is lust (lust). If you have lust, it's like your property (merit) being taken away by robbers (lust). Just like a tree trunk that has been hollowed out by worms and can no longer be used. It's like a tray of delicious food with a pile of feces on top, making people nauseous for up to three days.

Some people say: "oh, everyone has this lustful mind." That's right, because we have that lustful heart, we have to practice. If we no longer have desires, our original wisdom and light will appear. So "anasrava" is the place that practitioners want to go; That is the most precious thing a practitioner wants to obtain.

You must pay close attention! Among the six types of supernatural powers (Heavenly eye power, Heavenly ear power, Divine power, Other mind power, Live life power, Asrava-extinction power) What does this Asrava-extinction-power mean? That is, there is no longer any lust, there is absolutely no lust anymore. It should be said that we must "cut desire and eliminate love" (Cut off lust, cut off love), if we can cultivate to "pure fire" (mature practice), then we will be free. If we do not cut off desire and do not eliminate craving, we will always be controlled by ignorance and go crazy. From morning till night, I am not free and happy because my lust keeps destroying me.

Good-knowledgeable people! This is an essential place that we need to put special effort into. Because of it, we return to our original form, restore our original appearance, and attain endless wisdom; That source never runs out, it can't be used up, it can't be used up.

You need to develop the mind of bodhichitta to be able to break through the door of life and death. We must reflect and ask ourselves: Why do we need to believe in Buddha? Why do we want to become monks? Why do I not practice after becoming a monk? Why do we still have all kinds of delusions after becoming a monk? These are issues that we should not ignore. We must think clearly to escape the Three Realms, escape birth and death, and reach the peaceful Nirvana.

tieu_de: Cultivate Virtue - Create Karma
tom_tat: In everyday life, we are like someone who lives in passion and dies in dreams. Without cultivating any merit, how can one become a Buddha?
noi_dung:
Cultivate Virtue - Create Karma

In everyday life, we are like people who live in passion and die in dreams. Without cultivating any merit, how can one become a Buddha?

Think about it: Buddha in the past, by cultivating boundless merit, could become a Buddha.

Why haven't we become Buddhas? It's because we haven't cultivated boundless merit. My merit compared to His is so skewed. Because on one hand we practice, on the other hand we create karma; Therefore "The effort of cultivating is not equal to the karma created."

From morning to night we create body karma, verbal karma, and mental karma. Try examining your thoughts: One thinks that this person is not good and the other person is not good to you; Thinking that someone thinks this way and says that way towards you, so in your heart you create all kinds of karma of greed, anger, and ignorance. In the mouth, we also create karma, such as talking nonsense (someone is right and the other is wrong), or lying, saying embellished words, saying cruel things, saying things that poke at both ends, causing discord between one person and the other. There are people who go a day without talking about gossip, it's like a day they don't live. A day without telling lies is like a day without food. They feel very uncomfortable, so from morning to night they have to gossip and gossip in order for them to survive. Look, are these people strange? It really takes the effort to explain!

People who have bad habits do not admit their mistakes, but even cover up and cover up their crimes. Thinking that I don't lie, I don't have false thoughts, I don't have lustful thoughts, I wear a false mask to deceive others. Actually, in this life, how can we fool anyone? Not only can we not deceive others, but we also cannot deceive ourselves. Why so? Because when we have false thoughts, we try to ask if we know or not? If I knew, there's no way I could fool myself. If you can't fool yourself, how can you fool others? Only stupid people will deceive others.

People who do not truly practice will wear a mask, have a dark heart, do not follow the rules, do not do righteous things, but refuse to admit it. Therefore, in daily life, he is like a person who is born in passion and dies in a dream (drunken life and death dream). Without cultivating any merit, how can one become a Buddha? These people are hundreds of thousands of miles away from Buddha.

In other words, the merit that we cultivate is less than the karma that we create, which means "The gain is not as much as the loss." If you ask like that, how can we achieve it?

tieu_de: All Things Speak Dharma to You
tom_tat: In the Avatamsaka Sutra, it is taught that: "The Buddha manifests hundreds of thousands of sounds, as Sentient Beings expound the wonderful Dharma." That is, the Buddha manifests hundreds of thousands of millions of sounds to demonstrate the Dharma to Sentient Beings. We need…
noi_dung:
Everything Speaks Dharma to You

Only when you understand clearly will you be able to let go.

If you don't make it clear, you will always be attached.

In the Avatamsaka Sutra, it is taught that: "The Buddha manifests hundreds of thousands of millions of sounds, for Sentient Beings to expound the wonderful Dharma." Meaning the Buddha manifests hundreds of thousands of millions of sounds, to demonstrate the wonderful Dharma to Sentient Beings. We need to be enlightened to all the sounds in the world, because they are all the sounds of Dharma preaching. That:

Khe Thanh is the real square,

The colorless, pure body.

Meaning:

The roaring stream is the sound of a long, wide tongue,

Green trees are the shadow of the pure body.

The sound of the stream and creek is like the voice from the long, wide tongue of the Buddha expounding the wonderful Dharma; The green color of the mountain is also the color of the pure Dharmakaya, making those who see it feel happy. If you understand this philosophy, then everything in the world is speaking Dharma to you.

Good people speak good Dharma. Evil people speak evil Dharma. A horse says Dharma is a horse, a buffalo says Dharma is a buffalo. They make us understand the reason why we have the body of a horse and a buffalo. It turns out that these horses and buffaloes in their previous lives were not filial to their parents, not respectful to their teachers, or did not want to listen to their parents or teachers' teachings, turned their backs on their parents or teachers, so now they are born as animals, they have not changed much.

In short, if you maintain the Five Precepts and practice the Ten Virtues, you will be born as a human or go to heaven. When there is greed, anger, and ignorance, one falls into the three evil realms (hell, hungry ghosts, and animals).

The cat chases the mouse. The tiger chased the rabbit. The strong oppress the weak. Everyone spoke the Dharma to me. Everything has its Cause and Effect. Each thing has its own stance, telling the wonderful Dharma for us to hear. The teacher speaks the teacher's Dharma. Students speak the student's Dharma. The Bhikkhu preaches the Dharma of the Bhikkhu. The Bhikkhuni preached the Dharma of the Bhikkhuni. The conscious person preaches the Dharma, the inanimate person also preaches the Dharma. If you realize it, then the green mountains, the white clouds, the yellow flowers, the blue bamboo, all the myriad things all preach the Dharma to you.

Bandits steal other people's property because in the past they were robbed by others, so now they come to collect the debt. If he was not robbed by others in the past but now robs others, he will be robbed by others in the future. That's called repaying the debt (i.e. repaying the debt). This is the true principle of retribution in the cycle of Cause and Effect.

Therefore, as a human being, we must know "right great light, great merit and impartiality" (great merit means common work, impartiality means no selfishness or personal interests). In any place, at any time, we should not think about taking advantage of comfort and not accept loss. Actually, "tolerating losses is the way to gain comfort." Remember, ladies and gentlemen, remember. Don't try to take advantage of it, you have to give it to others and accept the loss. When we receive conveniences that we do not accept, we give them to others, then we are preserving our virtue.

Everyone must act according to their position and be dedicated to their position. Don't be greedy for things you don't deserve, don't drink too much alcohol. That is also the teaching of the Dharma.

Should say:

The pure and clear bamboo is the total body of the dharma body. The angry yellow flower has no non-paradise.

Meaning:

The green and blue bamboo reveal the Dharmakaya.

Sparkling yellow chrysanthemums are not Prajna.

We have to observe all things like that. Once you understand, let go of everything. If you don't understand, you will always be attached.

tieu_de: Don't Wait Until You're Old to Learn the Way
tom_tat: Born in this world, we must know how to practice quickly, don't wait. When you're young, if you don't practice and wait until your hair turns gray to practice, there's often no time left, so there's a saying
noi_dung:
Don't Wait Until You're Old to Learn Religion

Why have I still hesitated and refused to practice until today?

Born in this world, we must know how to practice quickly, don't wait. When you're young, if you don't practice and wait until your hair turns gray to practice, there's often no time left, so there's a saying:

Mac Dai wandered back to study Dao,

She is devoted to the young man.

Meaning:

Don't wait until you're old to practice,

The graves are deserted and the people are still young.

Even young people quickly go to death. The impermanent demon does not care whether the person is old or young, when the time comes, he will not be polite to anyone, he will drag himself to meet King Yama. So:

Duong Giang is no old man.

The underworld often meets each other.

Meaning:

On earth, no matter the old or young.

In the underworld, we often encounter each other.

You should pay attention: Time is very precious. "A little time is a little life." So don't arbitrarily let time go to waste. Waiting for the three disasters (fire, water, and wind) to come, can we avoid them? Therefore, when you are young, you need to practice diligently, don't wait until tomorrow to practice. Today, practicing immediately is the best policy.

Some people think: "Let's not practice today, wait until tomorrow to practice." But tomorrow comes, I promise again for tomorrow, promise again and again, until my head turns gray, my eyes are blurry, my ears are dull, my teeth are rotten. At that time, even though I wanted to practice, my limbs were no longer flexible and my body did not listen to me. At that time, the suffering was so immense!

You should remember that we live in this world like a fish lying in a small puddle of water, the water will soon dry up. There is a sentence:

The day is too late, the life of the heron is decreasing,

Like a small fish, private property is blissful;

The masses!

When you need to be diligent, it's like saving the first course; The thought of impermanence causes the kidneys to wander.

Meaning:

The day is over, life is gradually decreasing, Like a fish out of water, what's the fun? The masses!

Be diligent, like your head is burned,

Just remember impermanence, don't let it go.

For countless lifetimes up to now, we have not known how to practice, so we are born and then die, die and then born again, which is something that makes us feel very sad. Why to this day I still hesitate and refuse to practice? Think about it, time waits for no one, in the blink of an eye, your life has ended.

tieu_de: Tình Ái và Dục Vọng là Tảng Ðá Buộc Chân Người Tu Ðạo
tom_tat: Until your last breath, you should treat everyone well, but don't let love get in the way
noi_dung:
Tình Ái và Dục Vọng là Tảng Ðá Buộc Chân Người Tu Ðạo

Until your last breath, you should treat everyone well, but don't let love interfere.

In the karma of birth and death, love and desire are the root obstacles to the Way. As a person cultivating the Way, regardless of people or objects, if you give birth to craving, it will hinder your practice and prevent you from developing. To put it more clearly, desire is birth and death, birth and death is desire. Desire is the origin of birth and death. If we don't break through our ignorance of love and desire, we won't be able to get out of the great ocean of birth and death. How to escape birth and death? Very simple, just need " to cut off desire and eliminate love, " means to stop desire, except love, there is no other way.

People cultivating the Tao should not think about lustful love, much less should they engage in lovemaking. For anyone, you should not fall in love; As long as there is love, suffering cannot be avoided; Because having love makes it difficult to escape the cycle of birth and death.

Someone said: "Humans are emotional animals, eating, drinking and lust are natural." Because of that cause and effect, it is necessary to cultivate the Way. In the Four-Twelve-Chapter Sutra, it is taught that:

I see old people as my mother, older people as my sister, young women as my sisters and the little ones as my children. Please give birth to the heart to save them and eliminate evil thoughts.

As a cultivator, we must always contemplate like that. If we really don't have love, is it true that when we meet other people we just keep our mouth shut and don't pay attention to them? Incorrect! We are not attached to love, do not give birth to love, but do not give birth to hate others, nor can we say: "Because I do not love people, I must hate them." That is wrong. So what is right? That means neither loving nor hating anyone. Not loving or hating is the Middle Way.

What is practice? It is practicing the Middle Way. Always treat others equally and with compassion; But always be careful, don't fall into the trap of love.

You should pay attention! Don't be fascinated by love. If someone sends you a love letter, you feel happy, like a jumping rabbit, your heart is extremely happy, thinking that if someone loves you, it's a good thing. The truth is that the person who loves you only wants to drag you down.

You good-knowledgeable people should rely on this point to apply your efforts, you must truly understand that: "Love is an extremely troublesome thing." From countless eons until now, why can't birth and death end? It is because of the two words "love". If we can "cut desire and eliminate craving", then we can transcend the Three Realms and no longer have birth and death.

I love what I like, I hate what I don't like. Whenever I like it, it means I have given birth to love. Whenever you hate your heart, hatred is born. Both things, love and hate, are caused by emotions. Practitioners handle things without relying on emotions. However, it is not possible to be like Mr. Quan Cong, sitting on the processing table, people pay respects, but he does not even look. Towards others, we must be gentle and polite, we should not pay high tribute, be arrogant, or look down on others.

In short, we must have compassion for others and find means to help them. You should always think of others and make them happy. Until your last breath, you should treat everyone well, but don't let love interfere. Remember! That is an extremely important method.

tieu_de: Let's Make Efforts for World Peace
tom_tat: The current world is made up of many countries. Each country is made up of many families. Each family is composed of many people. Therefore, each individual has a great relationship with the whole world
noi_dung:
Make Efforts for World Peace

If the universe is full of righteous and peaceful energy,

the earth will not explode.

The current world is made up of many countries. Each country is made up of many families. Each family is composed of many people. Therefore, each individual has a great relationship with the entire world.

If the hearts of people in the world are pure and have no polluted thoughts, the world will definitely be peaceful without war. On the contrary, if people's hearts are polluted, the world will become evil. Everyone understands this principle but they do not practice it. Knowing and trying to make mistakes, that's truly pitiful.

The taste is good, the weak mind arises.

The taste is destroyed, the mind is free of action,

Meaning:

Good things are created by the mind.

Bad things are also done from the heart.

The world is now coming to a place of living in the morning but it is unlikely that there will be an afternoon. Why? Because the earth is about to explode, it is an extremely dangerous time. Why did the earth come to a breaking point? That's because "greed, anger, ignorance, " three types of evil energy pervade everywhere. If the earth is destroyed, humans can no longer exist.

However, people do not pay attention to studying this issue, live in confusion all day, and die in dreams. Letting time pass by in a confused way, not knowing that the dangers are overlapping. Some people only care about the immediate danger, but do not know how to think about the future. They are only worried that the human race will become more and more numerous, afraid that the Chapter will have no food to eat, no clothes to wear, no housing, no resources or fuel. They consider these issues to be important. Actually, those problems are still small, because by then, everything will naturally be resolved.

Actually, everyone's "birth and death" problem is the important one. One moment I'm still there, but the next minute I'm no longer there, in the blink of an eye I'll be gone. Death will come right over your head without you even knowing it. I pity people who are so indifferent to such a serious problem, treating it like a dream. "Where were we born and where do we go when we die?"No one knows. Even if I knew, what would I do? The only solution is "to turn evil towards good" (remove evil, do only good). Change yourself, don't be selfish or self-interested, but have compassion; for the benefit of all Sentient Beings and must learn the spirit of the Bodhisattva.

Everyone's behavior is controlled by the mind. Because of the mind, we transform into species in the ten Dharma Realms. A good feeling is born in heaven; One evil thought will result in hell. That:

With one thought, enlightenment attains Buddhahood,

One thought fascinates Sentient Beings.

Meaning:

One thought of enlightenment is Buddha,

A confused concept is Sentient Beings.

Simply put, when there is a thought of benefiting others, that is a Bodhisattva; a thought that benefits oneself, that is Sentient Beings. A thought that reflects back and finds answers within itself is Arhat

Bich Chi Buddha. An idea separate from enlightenment, rolling in the dust of life, is ordinary; a concept of leaving the dust of life to return to enlightenment, which is sainthood. So both sides rotate back and forth as easily as turning the back of your hand.

The world, good or bad, is created by a single thought in our mind. "If everyone has a good heart, the world will be at peace forever; If people have evil hearts, the world will be destroyed." That is a very obvious principle. Buddhism teaches people to do good deeds, knowing clearly Cause and Effect. Doing a lot of good deeds, doing a lot of merit, also means don't fight, don't be greedy, don't expect anything, don't be selfish, don't take personal advantage and don't lie. If so, the world will go from dangerous to secure. Therefore, it is said: "The mind is created by the mind alone." That is, everything comes from the mind. Mind creates the world, mind can also destroy the world. Mind creates heaven, mind can also create hell.

Families are made by people, people are formed by delusion. If bad delusions are changed into good delusions, then that person is a good person. If a good idea turns into a bad idea, that person is an evil person. That is the difference between evil people and good people.

We as practitioners must " Diligently practice Precepts, Concentration, and Wisdom. Eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance." That is the basic condition of practice. As a student of Buddhism, first of all we must "not do evil and do all good things." That is also the basic thing. If everyone followed this, the world would become a good place; Good energy will increase and evil energy will decrease. If the universe were filled with peaceful righteous energy, the earth would not explode.

How to make the world peaceful and peaceful? The only solution is to go and study Buddha's dharma where Bodhimanda has the correct dharma, then correct your mistakes to become a new person. If everyone abandons evil and does good, the world will not have three types of disasters and eight types of miseries. People all live in peace and love each other, no more fighting, no more greed. That is the universal world.

Hopefully at that time, people who have no belief or religion will also give up their greed for their family, their country, and the world, and do things that benefit society. We should also know that "assets are things outside the body." When we are born, we don't bring them, when we die, we don't take them with us.

When the darkness of evil people is dissipated by the light of good people, then the world will no longer be covered by evil energy, and the earth will not be destroyed. Although this principle is very simple, we must know how to apply it deeply to be effective. You should start from the "mind" to cultivate and improve the world, making the world peaceful.

Your leader is the "mind." If your mind is bad, your body will be full of diseases and encounter all kinds of unexpected accidents. We need to reflect, examine, and if we have sinned, we must quickly repent. Because:

Heavenly sin,

One repentance is easy to destroy.

Meaning:

Sin fills the sky,

One thought of repentance, everything will be cleared.

Of course, we must sincerely repent to be free of trouble. Don't take it as a joke, do evil things during the day, repent at night, believing that you can eliminate them. If you have such thoughts, not only will your sins not be eliminated, but they will also get worse. Why? I already know my crime, but if I try to commit it again, I cannot forgive it.
