tieu_de: Attacking Meditation Hall Must Be Extremely Strong
tom_tat: Today is the first day of Meditation Hall. I hope you make an effort to meditate. Don't waste the opportunity to testify
noi_dung:
Defeat Meditation Hall Must Defeat Chess Players

Need to sincerely meditate.

Having true bravery is what counts.

Today is the first day of Meditation Hall. I hope you make an effort to meditate. Don't waste the opportunity for enlightenment.

If you lose, you have to fight hard to prove it. You cannot sit on a meditation bed and have false thoughts. Thus, she only helps her with her meditation work. What are you delusional about? There are many different types of delusions, but in short, they are all delusions without boundaries. Some people have delusions like this: "This time, I will visit the Meditation Hall in the hope that I will be enlightened and will attain great wisdom. After I become enlightened, I will definitely announce this special news to the world, letting the whole world know that I am an enlightened person and making everyone respect me."

Think about it, is a person with such thoughts truly enlightened? I dare say that he is absolutely not enlightened! Why so? Because when I first sat down to meditate, I was already full of false thoughts. If not for the sake of fame, then it was also for the sake of profit. If you use effort for fame and profit, how can you achieve enlightenment?

Some people have delusions like this: "I will definitely be enlightened during this Meditation Hall! I will be the first enlightened person in this meditation course. Others are not enlightened, I am the only one who is enlightened, that is truly a very glorious thing!" There are even people who do not understand anything about enlightenment, pretending to be enlightened themselves. Everywhere he went, he claimed that he was enlightened, deceiving the masses and making them respect him. That's the " fisherman's pearl, " (rolling the fish's eyes so that others can mistake it for a pearl). Such childish thoughts are truly laughable. Hope you don't have those delusions. Must "step on the ground" means that your feet must stand firmly on the ground, and use meditation to have true strength, then that is significant.

Some people have such delusions: "I must definitely become enlightened; Once enlightened, people come to make offerings; If you make offerings, then you will build a big temple, become a dharma master, new followers will be close to you and make offerings and you will become a great dharma master famous in the world; Everyone knows that they have a high reputation." You must know that those who do not learn, are not talented, or do not know how to receive offerings cannot have a peaceful conscience.

Now talking about meditation posture, we need to sit correctly to benefit our body and mind. Otherwise, zazen has no value. While meditating, you must first let your body and mind be naturally gentle, do not rush or rush. It is best to sit in the lotus position, which is the basic position of meditation.

So what is cross-legged sitting (or cross-legged position)? That is, take your left foot to put it on your right foot, then put your right foot on your left thigh. That is the Vajra sitting position, meaning the position of solid immobility. In the past, Buddhas sat in the Vajra position and became Buddhas; This posture can subdue demons and restrain pagans. When they saw me sitting in this position, they immediately retreated, not daring to bother me again.

After sitting cross-legged, your eyes should look at the tip of your nose, neither looking east nor west. That's called:

Observe the eyes with the eyes, observe the mouth with the eyes, and observe the mind with the mouth.

Meaning:

Eyes look at the nose, nose towards the mouth, mouth towards the heart.

Only then can we maintain our body and mind; Take that mind that is running wildly and concentrate on it, don't let it run outside anymore. When this happens, it is called:

Specializing in all things,

Division is all bad.

Mean:

Single heart, new inspiration.

If the mind is scattered, it's deadlocked.

We need to sit respectfully, our spine must be straight, our head must be straight, neither bending forward nor falling back; Do not lean to the left or fall to the right. We must sit like a big bell, steady and not moving. Don't sit like a hanging bell, swinging it to the east and to the west. Sitting cross-legged is the most suitable posture for meditation.

Beginners will feel unfamiliar, with leg pain or back pain, so they shouldn't be considered important. We need to grit our teeth and endure, be patient for a long time, then naturally that phenomenon will no longer exist. That is called "9 sitting meditation", which means that if you sit for a long time, you will naturally have meditation, and you will naturally attain the taste of meditation.

What is called meditation? The taste of meditation means to attain the peace of meditation, to taste the gentle taste of peace. That taste is so magical that it cannot be described with thoughts or words. Just like when someone drinks water, he only knows whether it's hot or cold; I can't understand it with my mind, I can't use language to convey it. If you want to know whether the taste of meditation is sweet or bitter, you must make an effort to meditate. When you reach the corresponding realm, you will naturally understand that taste. So you must meditate. Being greedy until "water and stone appears" means that when the water dries up, the rocks will be exposed, and then we can taste the taste of meditation.

Meditation cannot be talked about, it requires participation. Therefore, Zen Buddhism does not establish written words, does not establish words, and is transmitted outside the canon. Directly point to the human mind so that you can see your nature and immediately become a Buddha.

A person who meditates, when he has reached enough of his fire pharynx, absolutely no longer gets angry, no longer argues with others, reaching a place called non-fighting samadhi. Nor do they seek fame or profit; Think of wealth as dew drops on a leaf, and fame as bubbles on a tile. In the moment of a dew drop, the water vapor will disappear. People who truly practice practice stay away from fame and profit; Don't sway your mind for fame and profit.

You want to test whether that person is truly practicing or not, to see if his mind is disturbed by fame and profit? If he fails to seek fame, he gets angry. If he fails to seek profit, he becomes angry, burning with ignorance, his nature is as fierce as a tiger, more ferocious than anyone else. Without having to ask, I know that he is definitely a man seeking fame and profit.

During the Qing Dynasty, Emperor Qianlong once went to Jinshan Zen Monastery in Tran Giang province to enjoy the scenery. At the Truong Giang River, the emperor asked Phap Thanh Zen Master: "On this river, how many boats pass each day?" The Zen Master replied: "There are only two boats passing back and forth." King Qianlong did not understand and asked: "How do you know that there are only two boats passing back and forth?" The Zen Master answered: "One boat is called nam, one boat is called name. is beneficial."

Because of this, I know that those who cross the river by boat, if not for fame, are also for profit. But they do not know that those who seek fame die for fame, those who seek profit die for profit. Finally, he pointed his empty hand to meet Mr. Pluto.

So:

Thousands of states treat you forever.

Only personal karma exists.

Meaning:

Anything can be brought.

Only karma is to follow forever.

If a person who practices Buddhism does not have anger and can be patient and endure suffering, it is easy to become a Dharma weapon. In Buddhism, he can be a person of good will, a pillar, and can spread Buddhism widely and widely. A practitioner who often gets angry is a person who destroys Buddhism, a person who harms the collective.

Buddhism has just arrived in the West (ie the United States) and planted Bodhi seeds in pure soil, which are now starting to sprout. I hope you are good gardeners, diligently water and fertilize to make them lush, then in the future the tall trees will bloom and bear Bodhi fruit.

People in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas need to pay attention to their speech, not to talk indiscriminately, not to talk nonsense at will. The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is a pure holy place to practice the Way, there cannot be the language of the leftist religion. You need to know that in the face of ten thousand Buddhas, how can you talk nonsense? You must remember!

Sickness is imported, disaster is born.

Meaning:

Illness enters through the mouth, disaster also comes out through the mouth.

This is a very wise quote; Whatever you say, you must think three times before saying it, to avoid saying things that are wrong with Cause and Effect. After speaking, we are not only responsible to the law, but also responsible to the Law of Cause and Effect.

Buddhism is a religion that promotes the spirit of "selflessness", so it does not accept fortune-telling, horoscope reading, feng shui, or physiognomy. Those things all go against Buddha-Dharma, so we must ban its dissemination. If you believe in those evil methods, then you will naturally accept that your "self" exists, it's all for you. Whenever I have my own things, I always find ways to calculate for myself, for myself and not for others; If so, there is no longer anything like Buddha-dharma.

Buddha-dharma teaches people not to fight, not to be greedy, not to seek, not to be selfish, not to seek personal gain, not to lie. As for feng shui, it teaches people to fight, to pray, to be selfish, to take advantage of themselves, and to lie. He even lied that in a hundred days he could become rich and become a mandarin. People who are greedy will immediately believe his words. In fact, great wealth has not yet been developed, but small wealth has already been wasted, because money has to be paid to the fortune teller. Fortune telling like that is like telling that person to rob a bank to get rich immediately. It doesn't take a hundred days to get rich.

Furthermore, if the fortune teller knows where there is good feng shui that can make you rich and get promoted, why doesn't he use it himself and tell others? What nonsense! I hope that smart people like you should not be superstitious and be deceived by those people.

Medicine, fortune-telling, astrology, physiognomy, and fortune-telling in Buddhism are among the five professions that practitioners should not do. He is a doctor who treats other people's illnesses (lay people can be doctors, but monastics cannot). Fortune-telling knows good and bad things. Star is the star that sees the stars and knows about good and bad things. General means physical appearance, which determines whether fate is favorable or unfavorable. Those are superstitions. We must know that the principle "humanity is determined to overcome heaven" is that humans can overcome heaven.

People who become monks and cultivate the Way are not afraid of life and death, let alone these small things? There's nothing surprising about those things. A person who is a monk is someone who has transcended his destiny.

Transcending the three outer worlds,

Not in the five elements.

Meaning:

Beyond the three worlds,

Not in the five elements.

If we calculate physiognomy and feng shui, those are the things that secular people believe. We must understand that human destiny is born from karma. Don't let your habits lead you, don't let your desires confuse you; You need to create your own destiny, you must be the master of your destiny. If you do a lot of merit, you will improve your destiny. When encountering trouble, it will naturally turn into auspicious. That:

Carrying out good deeds

Mac asked the progress.

Meaning:

Keep up the good work,

Don't ask about the future.

Now that I've reached Meditation Hall, I have to create a new life. Don't be superstitious, have true faith, don't follow what people say if you say yes then you'll be okay, then just follow others and they'll go first and you'll follow, that's very wrong. We must have Trach-phap-eye (eyes that can recognize the truth), know what is right and what is wrong, know how to distinguish good from evil, white from black; Only by clearly distinguishing ourselves will we not be bewitched by madness.

Zen practitioners can control their own life and death, living and dying very freely, without any restrictions. Should say:

Destiny depends on self, not nature.

Meaning:

My destiny is created by me, not by heaven.

King Yama himself cannot control him, he cannot do anything to himself. Why so? Because I have gone beyond the Three Realms.

What is coming and going freely? This means that when it comes to life and death, we are extremely free. If we want to live, we live, if we want to die, we die, whatever our heart desires. However, you must pay attention, this death is not due to suicide or self-drinking poison.

Your body is like a room. If you want to travel out, go wherever you want, then do so freely. If you want to transform into hundreds of thousands of millions of millions of millions of emptiness, transform the Dharma world to educate Sentient Beings, then accept your destiny at will. If I don't want to travel, I'll still stay in my room, no one can come and bother me. You should understand that the end of space transforms into the Dharma world, everything is in the dharma body, nothing runs out of this dharma body.

You are extremely diligent in suffering and meditating, constantly working day and night, just because you want to be free in life and death, to control your own life, to master the matter of life and death. Once you have mastered it, you have reached the realm of freedom of life and death.

The meditator reaches a place where he does not know there is a sky, below he does not know there is an earth, and in the middle he does not see anyone, and with the void they become one.

At such a realm, there will be a chance for enlightenment. Sitting and walking are all opportunities to open up wisdom.

I'm interested in the question: "Who is Nembutsu?"Who is Nembutsu? Who is reciting Buddha's name? Who is sitting here? Who is the person sitting here? When eating, who eats? When sleeping, who is sleeping? Must find that person. To seek all is Greed; Greed until the water and mountains end, then with a transformation you will become enlightened. That:

Mountains and waters are endlessly doubtless,

Willow teapot flowers are brightest in the village.

Meaning:

The mountains ended, the river stopped, I thought there was no way,

Willows, flowers, village decoration.

The mountains have ended, the rivers have ended, I think there is no more way. But behind the willow tree, behind the fresh flowers, a village appeared.

Again:

Hundred-chain-stem-heads are in full swing,

The world of the ten directions appears in its entirety.

Meaning:

At the top of a hundred-foot pole, take one more step, the world of the ten directions will appear.

If you don't sit in meditation, don't meditate, do you know where you were born, where you die, and where you go? You say you don't know. Not knowing means being born confused, then confused dies. A whole life like that is pitiful!

When people meditate diligently, when they become enlightened, they realize their original appearance before being born by their parents. Suddenly understand clearly; All the fine, rough, beautiful, and ugly things that are difficult for people to know, there is nothing in our mind that cannot be understood. When you reach the realm of great creation, you will become a Buddha in the future and reach the state of supreme enlightenment.

Lao Tzu once said the following two sentences:

The natural harm comes from the taste of beauty, the reason for evil.

The stage of understanding is good because it is good, and thoughts are not good.

Meaning:

People know that beauty is beautiful, there must already be ugliness.

Knowing that good deeds are good, there must have been bad things.

People all over the world know that doing good things is good, but when it comes time to do them, it's not good at all. People know that doing good deeds is right, but when the test comes, they cannot overcome it. Once again bewitched by the world, he cannot do good deeds but only runs away to do evil deeds.

People who study Buddhism know that "love, compassion, joy, renunciation, " the four immeasurable minds are the basis of Bodhisattva practice, but they refuse to do it. To know morality clearly, we must know how to use it? Study the Dharma every day "Six Levels," and when faced with challenges, you will not give alms, if you keep the precepts you will not keep the precepts, patience will run out of patience, diligence will cause you to lose diligence, meditation will not meditate, wisdom will also not have wisdom. You ask, what is the benefit of studying like that?

The following is the meaning of Luc-degree:

Giving alms: That is, using material assets or Buddha-dharma to give alms to others. Some people refuse to give alms when they need alms. On the contrary, he asked others to give alms to him, the more the better. Say I don't want to give you now, you need to give me alms! He always tries to take advantage and refuses to lose. This type of person always thinks they are right.

Upholding the precepts: Everyone in the world knows that keeping the precepts is keeping the precepts, but when faced with a challenge, not only do they not keep the precepts, but they also break the precepts. Taking precepts means not being moved. No matter what realm comes, I will not move. That:

Thai Son Bang was not startled at all.

Beauty is immobilized in the heart.

Meaning:

If Mount Thai collapsed in front of us, my heart would not be afraid.

The beauty before our eyes does not make my heart flutter.

That is the power of concentration that can change realms. Regardless of whether the scene is evil or good, favorable or unfavorable, I am calm; Without the mind of discrimination, the wind and waves will naturally calm down.

Patience: It means to endure what is not as desired. If you can endure all the things that are not according to your will, then that means you are willing to be tested and tested. If I can endure the test, I can pass "quan" (door). If I can't stand it, I won't be able to get through the door. Everyone knows that with patience, we will reach the other shore; But when the situation comes, you can't endure it. Flames of ignorance three meters high emerged; All the merit accumulated in one moment was completely wiped out.

Diligence: When you hit the Meditation Hall, you are diligent. Everyone wants to be diligent, but when it's time to be diligent, they refuse to be diligent, just want to lazily settle down and retreat, or run to make tea or intentionally go to the bathroom, or intentionally go to the kitchen to drink tea; These are all excuses to pass the time. When I hadn't yet entered Meditation Hall, I sounded very enthusiastic, saying that I would be very good at attending Meditation Hall. By the time Meditation Hall started, I no longer remembered what I had sworn before. Why so? This is knowing clearly and intentionally making a mistake. Even though I know meditation is a good thing, I'm still lazy. Do you think how to resolve such conflicting psychology? The rule of the meditation hall is that if anyone does not keep the rules, they will be beaten; Fight until you become enlightened.

Meditation: Meditating now is the best time to practice. Why is it necessary to visit Meditation Hall? Because we want our spirit to be focused, our mind free from false thoughts, allowing our wisdom to appear. Therefore, there is a sentence: "Wisdom of liberation" means meditation is a method of reaching time to attain realization (that is, setting a time limit to attain realization).

Wisdom: Is what takes us to the other shore, to escape birth and death. If you want to gain wisdom but are lazy, you will lose the opportunity to gain enlightenment. So when meditating, you need to be attentive and not let the time pass in vain because you don't know at what moment you will become enlightened. Some people have delusions like this: "I don't want to have wisdom because my ignorance is very good! It's okay if I don't understand everything." That's what's called: "Ignoring the spiritual path." It means ringing the bell while covering your ears (thinking no one hears), you're just fooling yourself.

Only when I die do I understand that I came to this world in vain.

At that time, it was too late to regret.

Buddhism in America is just starting, so there must be people who practice sincerely, must "practice", that is, really practice. We need to be single-minded in our practice, correct our own mistakes to practice, change our habit of practicing, and set an example for others so that the future of Buddhism can be bright. If, at the beginning, there were no true practitioners to serve as models, no one to develop the mind of Bodhi, then Buddhism in the West could not flourish. Therefore, the prosperity of Buddhism must be undertaken by young people.

Currently, the two "Three Steps One Bowing" are very sincere practitioners, it can be said that they are pioneers paving the way for Buddhism. Those people on the road, walked three steps and bowed once, not to pray for blessings for themselves, but to pray for peace in the whole world. Over the past two years, the two of them went hungry and thirsty, endured cold and heat, and endured the wind and rain with great hardship. Practicing like this is not something ordinary people can do. They endure things that others cannot endure, tolerate things that others cannot endure, eat foods that others do not want to eat, wear clothes that others do not want to wear. Regardless of whether the wind blows or the rain falls, he still bows to the Buddha continuously, regardless of whether it is hot or cold, hungry or thirsty, never stops, does not relax, is not lazy, recites sutras every day, morning and afternoon, every hour and every minute, never being lazy and settling down. Those two diligently tried to practice because they wanted Buddhism to develop everywhere in the world. The two of them practiced so hard, not for fame or profit, but because they wanted to take the responsibility of Buddhism as their own responsibility. That spirit is truly commendable.

You must learn to be equal to the merits of the two Three Bodhisattvas. Use them as a mirror to reflect. See what you have contributed to Buddhism, is what you do for yourself or for Buddhism? If it's for yourself, then feel extremely ashamed and immediately correct that inappropriate behavior. If it's for Buddhism, we need to make more efforts, we need to promote Buddhism to develop, protect Buddhism, we need to develop bodhicitta, practice the Bodhisattva path, always want others to be happy, not considering personal privacy, that is the spirit of the Bodhisattva path.

When you are in the meditation hall, when you walk and when you sit, you think it is miserable, but if compared to the two Three-Step One-Bow, that suffering is really extremely happy.

You need to experience this deeply, don't miss the opportunity. If those two practitioners did not develop the Bodhi mind and practice the Bodhisattva path, they would of course not be able to complete their journey.

You should not give birth to false thoughts in the meditation hall; The body is in the meditation hall but the mind is traveling to another world, that is, it is full of delusions, which can affect the mind of one's spiritual practice; You must remember! We must not let time pass by in vain, we must seize the opportunity, seize the opportunity for enlightenment. If you prepare like that, you won't be ashamed of yourself, otherwise it's just empty talk.

Lecture on August 20, 1979 at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas

tieu_de: Doing Just Enough is the Middle Way
tom_tat: The method of meditation needs to reflect light at all times, naturally. We must not be too hasty, nor too slow; there should be a saying
noi_dung:
Doing Just Enough is the Middle Way

If you fold it then it breaks, if it's slow then it loosens.

Not slow, not urgent to succeed.

The method of meditation needs to reflect light at all times, naturally. We must not be too hasty, nor too slow; there should be a saying:

Urgent willow ice, strong willow sect

Reckless and arrogant, success is achieved.

Meaning:

Tighten and break, slow and loose

Not slow, not urgent to succeed.

Not rushing and not being slow is the middle way; Walking, standing, lying, and sitting without leaving "this," far away from "this" means mistakes. "What is this"? That is the ultimate Middle Way.

Meditation must not go to extremes, neither too much nor too little; Too much or too little is not the Middle Way. Not falling into "emptiness," nor falling into "being,"not falling into the two boundaries, is called the Middle Way. It should be said: "The middle path is non-emptiness, non-existence" (neither emptiness nor non-existence), which also means true emptiness and wonderful existence. Don't be attached to emptiness, but don't be afraid of wonderful existence. True emptiness cannot be grasped, nor can it be abandoned. You can't grasp it, you can't let it go, that's the realm of true emptiness and wonderful existence.

People who apply effort need to have water in common (a beginning and an end) in order to achieve success. That: "Comprehend thoroughly and faithfully." It is impossible to practice one day and then rest for ten days. O one day, ten days of cold. O means one day of warmth, ten days of cold. Don't immediately retreat when encountering difficulties, go halfway and then give up. Such a person is a person without ambition. The ancients said:

Cultivating the Way does not violate arrogance, it only violates stationarity.

Meaning:

People who practice religion are not afraid of being slow, they are only afraid of standing in one place.

When you often meditate, you should pay attention to the first word, using the precious Vajrayana sword (ie wisdom) to cut off all delusions. When delusions are gone, wisdom appears. Only with clear wisdom can one destroy darkness and ignorance. Once ignorance is destroyed, we escape the Three Realms, end birth and death, and only then can we escape the circle of destiny (twelve causes and conditions).

People who diligently practice the Way need to have patience. No matter how difficult or difficult the situation is, you need to persevere. Only by being patient can we reach the other shore. So while visiting the Meditation Hall, don't be afraid of suffering. "Suffering until the end of the day" means the bitterness disappears and the sweetness returns. If I don't dive to the bottom, I will never rise to the top. Houses that are thousands of feet high are built from the ground, not built in the void. Therefore, it is necessary to meditate in the basic place, that is, to eliminate delusions. If we can stop thinking, then:

The mind is clear, the water shows the moon,

determined, immeasurable. Meaning:

The heart is transparent, the moon shows water.

Peace of mind, blue sky without clouds.

When the heart is at ease, a hundred misfortunes will disappear. The mind is calm, everything is peaceful.

That:

The mind only contemplates true wealth.

Lust destroys the field of merit.

Meaning:

If the mind stops and thoughts stop, then you will be truly rich.

If desires are exhausted, fields of blessings will be true.

Meditating means ending all delusions, leaving only the truth (eliminating falsehoods and remaining true). Just like sifting sand to find gold; Finding gold in the sand is very difficult. However, if you want to find gold, you must search in the sand, and you must have patience. Do you want to clearly understand your Buddha nature? Do you want to gain insight into your nature? So you have to practice patiently, meditate patiently, research, and over time you will certainly gain insight and enlightenment; "oh! So that's it."

When meditating, don't pay attention to other things, just keep thinking about the question "Who is Buddha's name?" You have to find that "Who", only when you find it will you stop meditating. Once your practice has reached a point of mastery, you will naturally reap good results.

When sitting in the lotus position, put your left foot on your right thigh, and put your right foot on your left thigh. That's because the left leg belongs to yang, the right leg belongs to yin. So when meditating, the left leg (yang) is above, the right leg (yin) is below, it is like infinity giving birth to tai chi, tai chi giving birth to duality (ie yin and yang). Even though it has such a meaning; But for convenience, you can leave your left foot below and your right foot above; Because the Dharma is not certain, it depends on each person's habits, there is no need to be attached to any fixed method or posture. Putting the left foot above the right foot is just a method, not an absolute rule; that you must obey like that.

In short, sitting cross-legged is the position where it is easiest to enter concentration. If we can enter concentration while walking, then sitting or not sitting is not a problem. The state when entering concentration is free from any delusions, a thought does not arise in the mind, and dust is not contaminated. If you can walk, stand, lie, and sit without giving birth to a single thought, without being polluted by worldly dust, then that is the time to put effort into it. You don't have to sit to be called meditating.

tieu_de: Buddhism is Very Equal
tom_tat: Buddha-dharma is very profound. When I'm within the Buddha-dharma I don't feel anything good, when I'm outside the Buddha-dharma I don't see anything bad either. However, in Buddhism, part merit and part sin are never wrong. Buddhism…
noi_dung:
Buddhism Is Very Equal

In Buddhism, a part of merit,

some sins never go wrong.

Buddha-dharma is very profound. When I'm within the Buddha-dharma I don't feel anything good, when I'm outside the Buddha-dharma I don't see anything bad either. However, in Buddhism, part merit and part sin are never wrong. Buddhism is extremely free and equal, there is no tyranny, nor does it go to extremes.

Why is it said to be extremely equal? Because all Sentient Beings, whether they are hell ghosts, ferocious gods, evil beasts, evil people or bad people, if they devote themselves to practice and return to their destination, they can all become Buddhas. Unlike the pagan theory that: "Evil people and bad people are forever evil, there is no way to save them. Or that the ferocious tiger beast, because of its extremely cruel nature, will not be saved."

During the Ming Dynasty in China, there was a Great Master named Lien Tri. He had a disciple, a tiger, who often stayed by his side to protect him. But because tigers are evil beasts, everyone who sees them is afraid. Therefore, the Great Master taught this tiger that every time he goes in or out, he must not go straight; The tiger immediately listened to His words and walked back and forth. So people are no longer afraid, because they know that the tiger is good. This tiger also knows how to go everywhere to create karma for Great Master Lien Tri. When people saw this good tiger coming, everyone competed to give alms and offerings. Therefore, tigers can also take refuge in the Three Jewels, protect and uphold the Buddha's teachings, and can become Buddhas.

Buddhism is extremely liberal, because the teachings in Buddhist scriptures only advise people to do good and avoid evil. If you do evil, you will receive your own retribution. But Buddhism does not force people to do good things, nor does it threaten that: "If you do not listen and create bad karma, you will be thrown into prison." Because everything is created by the mind, heaven or hell are created by our thoughts and karma. Buddha-dharma teaches people that: "The evil acts, the good ones obey." That means don't do evil things, just do all the good things, at the same time demonstrating the Cause and Effect principle, not being wrong even in small things like hair loss, so that people can realize the truth of transcending reincarnation.

tieu_de: Great Good and Great Evil are Beyond Fate
tom_tat: Once upon a time, there was a man whose last name was Lieu Pham, named Hoc Hai, a famous scholar in the Ming Dynasty. When he was young, he used to read books, but his father wanted him to study medicine to save people, so he immediately changed his mind to study medicine. After,…
noi_dung:
Great Good and Great Evil Beyond Fate

Destiny can be changed,

the ability to edit is in your hands.

Once upon a time, there was a man whose last name was Lieu Pham, named Hoc Hai, a famous scholar in the Ming Dynasty. When he was young, he used to read books, but his father wanted him to study medicine to save people, so he immediately changed his mind to study medicine. Later, he met a long-bearded general who told him: "You are destined to be a mandarin, you should read books to be able to become a great mandarin. On that day and that month, he will pass his baccalaureate; That year, that month, that day, he will be made a district official, with a lot of benefits, how much... Then that year, that month, he will be promoted to office, suddenly how much fortune... Until the age of fifty-four, on August 14, at midnight, he will die, without any children for the rest of his life." Therefore, Vien Hoc Hai changed his subject, and it was exactly as the math said, very effective. Because his destiny was already determined, he did not need to be diligent and did not seek progress. All day long, I just wander around the mountains and water.

One day he went to The Ha mountain, where there lived a Zen master named Van Coc. When he came to visit this Zen master; Zen Master Van Coc immediately gave him a cushion. The two sat facing each other like that for three days. The Zen master felt very strange and asked: "Where do you come from? Being able to sit motionless for three days and nights without any delusions, he must be a strange cultivator."

The Vien family replied: "Because everything is arranged by fate, I am neither greedy nor demanding, nor have any false thoughts."

The Zen master heard this and immediately continued: "I thought you were an extraordinary person, but it turned out you were just an ordinary person."

Hearing that, the Vien family was unhappy and asked: "Why does the Zen master say I am just an ordinary person?"

The Zen master replied: "If you are not an ordinary person, why are you bound by fate?"

The Vien family immediately asked: "Is it possible to escape destiny?"

The Zen master replied: "You are a scholar who reads books, how come you don't know that in the I Ching, there is a very clear saying: "The beast is jealous and hungry, " means go to good places, avoid bad places. If fate cannot be escaped, how can we reach a safe place, away from evil omens?

When the Vien family heard it, they were immediately enlightened and immediately changed their name to Lieu Pham.

said that from this day forward I am no longer an ordinary person. From then on, he always did good deeds, accumulated merit and virtue, so that what the fortune teller said was no longer valid. Vien Lieu Pham lived to be over eighty years old and had three children. Therefore, destiny is not certain, good and bad things are not certain. The ancients said: "The gentleman creates his destiny." A virtuous and upright gentleman can change his destiny and transcend his destiny.

Why do bad things happen? That's because our hearts are not good, we always plant evil things and of course we will reap evil rewards. If we can correct our mistakes, do good and avoid evil, then we can overcome jealousy and evil. From this, it can be inferred that destiny can be changed, and the power to change is in our hands. That: "Great good and great evil, beyond fate."

tieu_de: Please Bodhisattva Eliminate the Poison for the World
tom_tat: Why do we attack Ksitigarbha? Because there are so many disasters in the world right now, we need Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to use the power of his original vows to eliminate all disasters.
noi_dung:
Please Bodhisattva To Detoxify The World

Using nectar and French water to purify toxic gases in the world.

A part of the poison, a part of the world's peace.

Why do we attack Ksitigarbha? Because the world currently has too many disasters, we need Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva to use the power of his original vows to eliminate all disasters.

Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva highly respects filial piety, because he has always been a filial child to his parents. This is not an easy thing, because it was from suffering and hardship that he attained enlightenment. His parents did not believe in the Three Jewels, but He had to comply with their wishes, using all skillful means to persuade them to have righteous faith in the Three Jewels. Wherever he went, he performed Bodhisattva actions, without revealing his appearance, without attachments. There is no form because he does not count his merits and does not personally praise his virtues. Just like when saving Sentient Beings, He said that Sentient Beings saved themselves and did not want Sentient Beings to thank Him or pay homage to Him.

When he was in the position of Bodhisattva, he did not think that he was superior to other Bodhisattvas; Either we have great vows, great compassion or the most generous supernatural powers. He doesn't have those thoughts. All of His actions, every move, every word, every conduct, are considered as nothing: Things we do with all our heart and soul but do not see that we have done them, do not give rise to pride, and do not attract the attention of others. He only thought that it was His duty, He did not list his merits, so He touched all Sentient Beings, causing them to praise Him and even Buddha praised Him. Buddha does not arbitrarily praise others, only when there is someone worthy does Buddha praise. Because Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva does not count his merits, nor does he propagate his merits, he is inspired to communicate. That induction of communication is not achieved by using tricks or trickery. It comes naturally. We practitioners of the Tao must learn the boundless spirit of Ksitigarbha's vow:

Hell is empty, one cannot become a Buddha.

Sentient Beings reach the end, attain Bodhi.

Meaning:

Hell is not yet empty, I swear I have not yet become a Buddha.

Sentient Beings are completely liberated, only then will they attain Bodhi.

Every year we retreat, because we want the world to eliminate toxic gas. Currently, the air is very polluted, the universe is full of toxic gases, and all methods cannot eliminate it. The only way is that we must be sincere and pray to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas to release light, eliminate those toxic gases, and make those invisible and invisible toxic gases disappear. So in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas, every action is related to the safety of the entire world. In this Bodhimanda, if you are not sincere, the world will become more dangerous!

Humanity creates too much negative karma and it is difficult for human strength to eliminate them. Today, on the day of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva's soul, we are of one mind, with utmost sincerity, reciting " Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva"; hoping that he can be moved by the Bodhisattva's compassion, allowing him to help the world reach a place of peace and safety. Whether or not you get this inspiration depends on your sincerity. One person's strength is not enough, we need the strength of the masses. Therefore, it is said: The masses are sincere, unite their minds and join forces, together praying for world peace.

Now you understand in your mind that this world full of disasters has no peace. That's why Bodhimandas all over the world are praying for peace. First, it was proposed by the Buddhist Lecture Hall and Kim Son Thanh Tu, then other places in Hong Kong and Taiwan followed suit; That also proves that the world is falling into a very difficult and dangerous situation. However, the true bridge for world peace is Bodhimanda in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. Why so? Because any dharma conference held here does not expect to have great benefactors coming to donate money, it is held quietly every year; Every day and hour is organized. It doesn't matter whether there is a master son or not; Just proceed as usual, considering it your duty, without pride, without the slightest calculation of benefits or harm. I just hope that Buddha will release light to soon eliminate all the toxic gases in the world. Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva used nectar and consecration to make Sentient Beings' ears and diseases disappear, and sins and blessings were eliminated. Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva uses his generous vows to help Sentient Beings escape suffering and attain happiness, dispelling all disasters and obstacles. Reciting Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva means helping the world to be detoxified, but there is no need to use antiseptic drugs, just use nectar water to eliminate poison in the world. Spend a little more and the world will have a little more peace. When the toxic gas is no longer there, then Sentient Beings will enjoy blessings and humanity will be at peace!

Lectured on September 4, 1982, on the occasion of the Tripitaka at the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas.

The Irresistible Unsuccessful Direction

If you can't bear it, you have to try to be patient. Don't be afraid of pain, don't go around in circles. Otherwise, concentration will not be achieved.

During the Meditation Hall, everyone must understand the meditation hall rules. No one is allowed to run or walk until they have played. If you don't keep the rules, if you don't listen to orders, you're breaking the rules. In the meditation hall, there are rules of the meditation hall. After the initiation, the monk Duy-na had to look to see if everyone had put on their shoes, then knock once. Waiting for everyone to stand up, teacher Duy-na then played two more sounds on the gong. The two gongs have not yet been sounded, even though everyone has stood up, no one is allowed to leave. That's a very simple rule. You must understand it. If you just declare purity and start playing right away, but you haven't stood up yet, what will you do? It's okay if I have to wait another three minutes. Because there are many people who sit for a long time and their legs get numb. If they can't stand up, what should they do? That is very common knowledge in the meditation hall that you need to understand.

I know many people who sit for a long time and their legs get numb and cry. Crying is of no use. The more you cry, the more it hurts. The leg doesn't say: "If you cry, the pain will go away!".

Many people think that meditating is a very good thing. In fact, meditating is to patiently endure suffering. "The better" means "the more miserable" is. Everyone here woke up at 2:30 a.m., only had one hour during the day to rest and then continue practicing until twelve o'clock at night. Only sleep two or three hours a day. That's using effort and forgetting your own life. It can also be said as "Let go of death and be reborn" (throw away death, exchange for life). That:

Let go without ever dying, without ever being born again,

Let go of the false impermanence and become the true imperishable one.

Meaning:

Can't let go of death,

How can you change your life?

Can't get rid of the fake,

How can it become real?

If you cannot endure suffering, how can you enjoy blessings? So if you want to get to the place of true practice, you have to be patient and work hard, grit your teeth and endure the pain. Actually this pain may not be painful. But because I want to hurt, it hurts, it forces me to suffer. "The patient cannot endure the pain of this leg.". When it hurts, if you can't be patient, it's like you can't overcome the challenge. I definitely want to destroy it with my whole body, all my organs. "Organ" refers to the suffering of the body, or indicates pain, or indicates affliction. If at the moment of pain you can endure it without causing trouble, that is kung fu. If you can't endure it, then you can't pass the test. Some people come here and can't stand it even for a day, they just want to run away. You have now passed many days, it is not a trivial matter.

Most girls are afraid of foot pain. But being able to endure such suffering here means that deep good roots have been planted, and in the future this seed of Bodhi will definitely sprout and achieve results. Therefore, it is said that "infinite effort" means that the work is not in vain, the more effort you put in, the more you will achieve, there is no fear of wasted time.

Cultivation requires "forbearance", which means patience with things that are difficult to endure. "Forbearance of Dharma" is patience with the arising and passing away of the characteristics of dharmas. If you can't endure it, you have to try to be patient, don't be afraid of pain, don't go around in circles, otherwise you won't be able to achieve concentration. The most important thing is to see that all Dharmas are empty, see clearly and let go. From the place of birth of patience and the dharma of patience, we will realize the dharma of non-birth of patience. That is called "Not seeing any Dharma arising, Not seeing any Dharma passing away." Meaning: Not seeing any Dharma arising. I don't see any Dharma being destroyed.

tieu_de: When Immersed in the Taste of Zen, Everything Goes Wrong
tom_tat: When meditating, don't be greedy for the taste of meditation. What is Zen taste? That is the happy feeling of meditation. Sitting for a long time, you will naturally feel very free, comfortable and extremely happy. If I take…
noi_dung:
When Immerse myself in the Taste of Zen, Everything Goes Wrong

I'm just waiting for the Zen master to come,

once you wait, you forget to put in the effort.

When meditating, don't be greedy for the taste of meditation. What is Zen taste? That is the happy feeling of meditation. Sitting for a long time, you will naturally feel very free, comfortable and extremely happy. If we are greedy for that state of freedom and happiness, it will not be easy to progress. I will stop and just start thinking about finding that Zen position again. If that realm has passed, then seek and ask: "When will I have such a realm again? In that realm of no-cause, no-self, no-sentient beings, no-life, no-worry, no-brains, completely free and peaceful, when will I be able to get it again?..." When I wait for this meditation to come, I will forget the effort, this is called attachment to the meditation.

People who meditate need to be free from troubles and obstacles, without greed and desires, without joy and worry, without terror and fear. You should consider your body as nothingness in the Dharma world, there is no need to be attached to greed or desire. If you are greedy, you will fall into the second meaning.

Here are the four realms:

First Zen Thien, Leaving Birth, Joy and Bliss: This means that we will be able to separate ourselves from the afflictions of Sentient Beings, obtain the food of meditation, be filled with the Dharma of joy and peace, get out of the confusion of Sentient Beings and move towards the path of enlightenment of the saints. To reach this state of meditation, one cannot pretend to do so, one cannot say it oneself, but must be certified by a wise person.

This realm has a way to prove it: That is, when your breath stops and you no longer breathe, but it is not death, this is entering concentration or entering first meditation. This first meditation is completely different from sleeping, you should not think that sleeping means entering concentration. Sleeping not only means breathing, but many people also snore loudly, making it sound like thunder to others. Therefore, whether your breathing has stopped or not, good and knowledgeable people will know immediately. Someone said: "I feel like I can no longer breathe." That is fake, that is impersonation. If I knew, I still wouldn't have entered the first meditation. So you can't sell fake brands.

If I wanted to analyze it thoroughly, I'd have to write a whole book. If you talk too much, it will create obstacles for you. Let's just say a little, to avoid you from giving birth to the false view that you have entered the first meditation; Treating yourself like that means deceiving others.

Second Zen Heaven, Concentration of Birth, Joy and Bliss: This realm is one step higher, not only is breathing stopped, but the heart pulse also stops. This realm is not something we can know or talk about. If we say we have reached that realm, then how can we feel it? Surely I have never entered samadhi, and then impersonate myself to deceive others?

Tam Thien Thien, Ly Hy Dieu Dieu Land: When reaching this realm, breathing and heartbeat stop, even thoughts are no longer there. When we reach this realm, we will be free from joy, let go of meditation, and no longer be absorbed in anything. This realm is much higher than the first and second meditations. At that time, every strand of my hair also felt unusual joy, my eyebrows and eyes were smiling with immense joy.

Four Heavenly Meditations, Equanimity of Thoughts on the Pure Land: At this point everything is empty, "one unborn thought is fully manifested" That means when a single unborn thought arises, the true nature of the mind is revealed. Get there:

Heavenly water resembles water, sky and moon.

Thousands of miles, thousands of thousands of thousands of miles.

Meaning:

Ponds and lakes with thousands of water, thousands of moons appearing.

Ten thousand miles without clouds, ten thousand miles of green.

In this realm, everywhere the Dharma is preached to us. Because "Flower flowing water represents Maha," means falling flowers, flowing water like saying Mahayana Dharma. We don't know this realm, and we shouldn't say: "I have reached the Four Heavens." If so, I will give birth to great arrogance and say extremely deceitful words. This also requires a good and knowledgeable person to confirm it for you to be correct.

Why are good-minded people called people with bright eyes? Because that person can look and know immediately what level his practice has reached. If you want to test Him, then just try it! He doesn't care about that at all. If it is truly good knowledge, there is no way we can test it. He did not immediately speak out because he was asked. As long as we get close to Him after a long time, He will tell us. But it is not certain that He made it all clear. Sometimes He used examples or just preached a few simple sentences. That's why we can't go everywhere and beat bells and drums and say: "I have become a Buddha!" Saying that is extremely deceitful and a farce. In the future, you will fall into hell and have your tongue cut out. That is extremely pitiful.

tieu_de: Good Ashrams are Hard to Find
tom_tat: From countless lifetimes up to now, we have created too many sins and bad habits. Not knowing how to repent or practice, bad habits increase day by day, wisdom decreases day by day; Karma is getting worse day by day.…
noi_dung:
Good Ashrams Are Hard to Find

If you want to practice without meeting a good Bodhimanda, you cannot practice.

From countless lifetimes up to now, we have created too many sins and bad habits. Not knowing how to repent or practice, bad habits increase day by day, wisdom decreases day by day; Karma is getting worse day by day. Because of these reasons, it is not easy for people to practice; Wanting to learn to become a good person is also very difficult, wanting to become a monk is even more difficult, because of all kinds of adversity and karma. When in the human world, we are ignorant and do not know, so we create a lot of karma, without fear of Cause and Effect retribution. So now if you want to practice the Way, all kinds of karmic obstacles come from everywhere, and all kinds of obstacles arise. Some people don't allow it because of their family circumstances, some because of their country, and some people because of their attitudes, actions, or jobs create all kinds of obstacles, not allowing them to practice.

Therefore, wanting to truly cultivate the Way is as difficult as wanting to go to heaven. However, even though it's so difficult and miserable, why don't you practice? No! The more suffering we have, the more we have to practice, we have to do things that are difficult to do. If we don't start in a miserable and difficult place, we will never be able to completely eliminate karma. Therefore, we must practice patience; must endure things that no one else can endure, give in to things that no one wants to give in, do things that no one else is willing to do, eat things that no one wants to eat, endure things that no one can bear. Just like that, over time, merit will increase, sins will decrease, wisdom will increase, and karma will gradually disappear.

Because in the past, karma accumulated little by little. Now, little by little, it's getting easier. Just like when it's cold, it gets colder and colder, until winter is extremely cold, then it starts to get warm again. However, you can't get warm immediately, you have to slowly warm up one day at a time, then warm up again in the summer. The hot season is like a time when we no longer have obstacles; The cold season is like the time when karma is still deep.

Now we practice, meditate is good, chant Buddha's name is also good. No matter what Dharma you practice, you need to find something to do, don't let your mind be empty, because it will still think aimlessly and have delusions. Constant Love

The most harmful thing in life is deep love.

The noblest thing is to practice pure religion.

You see, this tree has two branches, parallel to form one, the upper branch and the lower branch are combined together, do you know what that is? This is because countless lifetimes ago there was a couple who loved each other very deeply. Those two people made a vow: "In heaven, I vow to work with the winged bird. On earth, one vows to connect with one another." This means that if born in heaven, they will become lovebirds with two wings next to each other. If born on earth, they vow to become a tree with attached branches. This man and woman were very loyal, so they became husband and wife. Both people have the same hobby: love of money. Men sacrifice their lives to make money, women like to waste money, so reciprocity is very compatible.

However, because they love each other so deeply, their karma is also very deep. Life after life, one is born in hell, falls into the animal world, becomes a hungry ghost, and finally falls into hell. Up to now, this couple has turned into herbs. This tree should have two branches, but they grow in the same place, so they are forever bound together and will not be separated. You see, the left branch surrounds the right branch, and the right branch also rushes to hug the left branch, like a man and a woman hugging each other. That's how we see that this man and woman have had a very deep habit of being infatuated with love and paralysis for many lifetimes. Nowadays, they have become herbs, but they still cannot get rid of that love. Between these two roots there is a stone, which these two people value as precious jewels. What is that rock? It turned out to be the bank account of those two people in their past lives.

A few years ago, we once went into the city to preach the Dharma. When passing by the riverbank, I saw this tree stump and immediately picked it up and brought it home. You look: the top of this tree was cut off, the roots were also cut off, revealing two very dry branches, but these two branches still hugged each other tightly. Don't you find that pitiful?

I cannot believe this Dharma teacher, because it has no proof and is not reasonable. Basically, I want to scare children, just talk about dreams." It's up to you to believe it or not. I have no way to make you believe it because this is a very difficult Dharma to talk about and preach. People who are addicted to love, no matter what you say, they still won't wake up and won't be able to accept it. The most harmful thing in the world is deep love. The noblest thing is to cultivate purity. It's not that people don't know that reason; I know but I try to commit it because there is no way to break the habit I have done in many previous lives.

There is a Chinese proverb that says: "When he already holds a dry firewood in his hand, he is reluctant to give it up to exchange it for a flower branch." This is an example of people who are always attached to love. If we tell them that giving up those attachments and cultivating the Way is more valuable, they will certainly be stubborn and not want to turn back. That:

It's raining and pouring water everywhere,

but it is difficult to freshen and grow rootless grass.

Buddha's door is vast,

tieu_de: Meditation: Meditation First Needs to Build the Foundation
tom_tat: Some people who study Buddhism like to meditate, some like to study Sutras, preach the Dharma, study Vinaya, Tantra or Pure Land Buddhism. Regardless of which sect you like, you need to persevere in your determination and practice diligently to become successful...
noi_dung:
Meditation: Meditation First Needs to Build the Foundation

The foundation is unstable, the house will shake,

When the wind blows, you fall, when there is heavy rain, it collapses.

Some people who study Buddhism like to meditate, some like to study Sutras, preach the Dharma, study Vinaya, Tantra or Pure Land Buddhism. Regardless of which sect you like, you need to persevere in your determination and practice diligently to achieve success.

If you're not single-minded, you'll learn nothing. I meditated for two and a half days but thought I wanted to recite Buddha's name, half a day after chanting Buddha's name I wanted to study the Law, not long after studying the Law I wanted to study Tantra; The target disorder is not the most specialized. Why can't I specialize? Because I'm still pursuing outwards. My feet step on two boats at the same time, I don't know if going up to Giang Bac is good or going down to Giang Nam? So, my whole life I'm still confused.

Therefore, when meditating, you must always be diligent, don't be lazy for even a second, and be greedy until:

Mountains and waters are endlessly doubtless,

Dark willow blooms in every village.

Meaning:

The mountains ended, the river stopped, I thought there was no way,

Willows, flowers, village decoration.

That means we will see a different sky, we will see the wonderful wonders of nature. But we need to meditate to the extreme, to the point where "is crowned to create the extreme" means to reach the highest peak, to reach the ultimate point to have a little hope; But that hope is not much. Even though there is a little hope, don't get attached to that hope. Otherwise we will create more trouble, that is, cling to something that has no meaning at all. To meditate means to be sincere and diligent.

First of all, we must train our feet to obey, not to cause trouble or cause pain. How to stop my feet from hurting? Is there any mantra to chant to relieve leg pain? Or maybe I have to take some medicine to make my legs hurt less. That's not it! I need to go through that pain for a while, then gradually my legs will obey and the pain will go away. If you can't endure the pain and change your leg as soon as it hurts, your leg will never listen to you; Because I pampered it too much. When my leg hurts, I have to scare it like I would a child. If parents love and do not let their children suffer, then those children will not be able to endure suffering in the future. My leg is like a child's, I'm afraid it will hurt and it will always hurt. When my leg hurts, of course I feel pain. When my leg doesn't hurt, I also feel pain because I have trained it to have a bad habit.

We have to train our legs and back to listen to us; so that they no longer hurt or ache; Then your eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind all listen to your words, and these six senses no longer run out to pursue them. Don't be swayed by sight, sound, smell, taste, touch, or dharma. Not being moved by the six senses and the six senses is knowing how to use effort. So say:

The eye contemplates the non-existent internal form and form.

The ear hears and hears the mind without knowing.

Meaning:

The eyes see shapes but the heart doesn't care.

Don't know double mind sound headphones.

I have to often reflect back. Don't pursue external things, always stick to the basic method, that is, talk to the beginning "Who is the one who recites the Buddha's name?" That means how to grasp the root, don't run after the tip. Regarding small detailed issues, don't let your mind worry, then you will gradually understand everything.

When practicing meditation, if you don't know how to practice sitting cross-legged or half-lotus firmly, you should not be eager to learn how to meditate. Because the foundation is not solid yet! Therefore, we must first build a good foundation before meditating.

Like the first week, I had to level the ground. To build a house, you must first clear the land and trample it out.

In the second week, the foundation must be laid. Building a foundation takes a lot of effort; That is, we must practice patience: endure pain, endure hunger, endure thirst, endure cold; Whatever the situation, we have to endure it. Although this is a laborious task, it is an inevitable thing to do. The land needs to be leveled and the foundation needs to be built firmly so that the house can be built solidly. If the wind blows, the house collapses, or the rain pours and the house falls apart, it means the foundation is not solid, the foundation is not stable.

By the third week, you can build poles, pillars, rafters, pole frames, and oars.

After the fourth week, build walls, fix doors, close windows, and roof tiles. That's the order of building a house: We can't "Just dig a hoe and dig a well". There's nothing you can do that's instantly successful.

The same goes for meditating or reciting Buddha's name; Studying the Teachings, cultivating Secrets, and practicing the Vinaya are all like that. That means you have to pay close attention. The mind must be sincere, don't be greedy for far-fetched things, don't listen to people saying Tantra is good, then follow Tantra. Don't be foolish and confused, until you die you still won't wake up. If I don't accept the evidence in front of me, then I'm really in love with it too much. Honey, honey, I don't know why, suddenly I die. What a secret. Therefore, honey is truly delusion. (These two words are pronounced the same in Chinese) U Very confused.

Those who study Buddhism need to study the truth and not blindly follow it. We need to: "Be close to virtuous people, stay away from people." Meaning that we need to be close to virtuous people and stay away from evil people. Evil people are people who specialize in deceiving people. People with virtue do not deceive anyone. Unscrupulous people always use cunning tricks; How can there be virtue? Only those who do not deceive will have more and more merit; Only then can virtue exist. You must observe and judge others in this aspect. Don't look at the outside and say: "Oh! I find that guy very virtuous, truly a wise man." Actually, it's not authentic, because you must know what that guy's background is? Understanding clearly is what counts.

In the Dharma Ending Age, people all suffer from the common disease of talking about far-fetched things, using their ears instead of eyes, hearing what others say is good and immediately running after them. Running like that doesn't matter whether it's good or bad, even being deceived by people and still not waking up. Learning about superstitions about talent, feng shui, and fortune-telling are all extremely pitiful things.

Today I read in the newspaper that in Phuoc Kien province, Mainland China, there were six children who escaped to the sea and committed suicide to become fairies. What is the reason? It's because heretical doctrines deceive people's hearts. They say that if someone does evil, he becomes a devil, if he does good, he becomes a god or fairy. What is a good thing? Don't be afraid of death. Because in remote villages, many children are very honest and spontaneous, so when they hear that, they immediately believe it. Believing that good people are not afraid of death, and that when they die, they can become fairies, so these six children committed collective suicide in the hope of becoming fairies. They think that "In the past there were eight fairies, probably by mass suicide. Now we need to commit collective suicide to become six immortals, to avoid drifting into the six paths of reincarnation." So they committed collective suicide to become immortals.

Can they become immortals? I can prove that they are not fairies. Why don't they become fairies? Because they are extremely delusional. People who become immortals are very intelligent and not stupid. There is no fairy who does not understand the truth, does not know right from wrong. How did they commit suicide at the same time to become immortals? If becoming an immortal is so easy, why don't the masses quickly commit suicide to become an immortal? This is impossible. Those country people are extremely pitiful. Blindly believing in evil doctrine causes children to die unjustly. This is a truly pitiful thing.

Now I ask, why are the children not afraid of death and want to become fairies? It was because of pressing circumstances. Seeing that human life is no better than death. What does it mean to be a walking piece of meat? That's why we found a way out: collective suicide. Those six children wrote on paper the word "Tu" thousands of times. Every day I write the word death, death, death... From morning to afternoon I keep thinking about the word death. Therefore, these children are foolish, deceived by superstition and completely forget the right goal and direction.

As Buddhists, we should not be superstitious but must eliminate superstition. What is superstition? That means being ignorant, listening to what people say without thinking. I believe everything people say, vaguely, so it's called superstition. Superstition is not scary, the scariest thing is believing in superstition, believing in crazy pagan things. There are people who consider themselves smart, but do not believe in true things, but when they encounter false things, they immediately believe, that is delusion within delusion. They do not perceive the truth, consider the truth to be false, consider the false to be true. Just like those six children, who wanted to die to become fairies. It was a method to deceive people, but those six children believed it. If we teach them that only by cultivating they can become immortals, I'm afraid they won't believe it. Therefore, in the world there are many pitiable people and countless regrettable things. A word that is difficult to fully express.

tieu_de: Light and Sound Heaven and Science
tom_tat: Question: Buddhism says: "The ancestors of mankind came from Quang Am Heaven." Is this a contradiction with scientific reasoning? For example, science has the theory of evolution, which says that humans evolved from a microbial state...
noi_dung:
Light and Science

Science does not exist. Because I call it science, it is science.

Question: Buddhism says: "The ancestors of mankind came from Quang Am Heaven." Is this a contradiction with scientific reasoning? For example, science has the theory of evolution, which says that humans evolved from the earliest microscopic state, went through countless billions of eons, slowly evolved, and finally turned into monkeys and then into humans. Is this consistent with Buddhist principles?

Answer: Humans came from the Light Heaven; But not from seven billion million years ago, perhaps even seven billion million years ago they existed here. The gods of Quang Am Heaven who came to the human world are not perfect people but have lost their wisdom. Why? It's just like when we are reincarnated and born. In the beginning, when the world did not have humanity, was not yet civilized, it was all chaos (like a chicken egg). The gods flew to this world, crowded like flies, thinking that there was delicious food here. Those people came down from Quang Am Heaven and probably traveled for a very long time before reaching Earth, just like a rocket launched into space, flying into the orbit and spending many years before coming here. The gods come to earth for no special purpose. They traveled, then lost their direction, so they came to earth in a panic. After coming to earth, they are no longer as intelligent as they were in heaven. They only have one type of awareness left, unlike when they were in heaven. Just like humans are inherently intelligent, but when they die and are reincarnated as children, they forget all about the past. Just like a person who crashes a car, falls unconscious, and is no longer aware of anything.

Although it is said that they came down from the Light Heaven, they gradually lost all their existing virtues and wisdom, leaving only a little bit of awareness. Even though they came down from heaven, they were only a few, no one knew how many. There is no history to interrogate, and the time is too long ago, so there is no way to verify it.

What we call "science, " is not science at all. This is just a noun, I named it "science." In fact, it is just a kind of theory, reason. Is that theory complete or not? Must rely on your interpretation and understanding capacity. Many of you have a very broad understanding. But there are others who have not studied science and do not understand what science is. Is it true that people who have not studied science have no ability to reason? Not! Regardless of whether one studies or not, each person's nature has the ability to reason. Don't say that only by studying science can there be science (understanding science). If you haven't studied science, there is no science (not understanding science). Just like Buddha nature, it is available to everyone.

Science is only a small part of Buddha nature. It is not the most perfect theory. You say that people do scientific research like that, and write their thesis like that; Actually, it's just a crazy human attachment. Just like "puts a head on his head" (doing things with attachments, useless, paradoxical). There is no need for anything, but trying to find work around the clock. I was busy searching forever, but couldn't find anything. Even with scientific research and endless research, they cannot come to a real conclusion.

People are too attached to science, thinking it is the best. In fact, everything is available in our own nature, there is no need for us to look outside to look for it. When you look outside, you will never find it. You said you found it. Oh, it's true; But it's just a fake. Because the real thing cannot be found or talked about. Science does not inherently exist (has no entity) because we name it science, so we call it science.

tieu_de: Nature, Consciousness, Mind, Mind
tom_tat: Not being influenced by external circumstances, that is practice. Being transformed by external circumstances means falling
noi_dung:
Nature, Consciousness, Mind, Mind

Not being influenced by external circumstances, that is practice. Being transformed by external circumstances means falling into hell.

Question: How are nature, consciousness, mind and mind different?

Answer: Just as a newborn baby is very carefree, has no concept of himself, Sentient Beings, or lifespan, then that is also like "Tanh." When a baby knows how to breastfeed, that is like "Consciousness". After drinking breast milk, I know how to wear a shirt. If I don't wear a shirt, I feel cold and feel ashamed; then feel hungry, thirsty, cold, hot, then that stage is like "Idea." Until you grow up, at that time you want this or that, that is "Tam". These are four types of mind, but it can also be said to be one, they are interrelated and cannot be separated, because they are the same family. Although they are four different nouns, their nature is the same. "Karma" is the basic consequence they create.

Now to expand a bit, what is called "Buddha." "Nature" which is Buddha. What is God? "My consciousness" is god. "I" is the discriminating mind and "Tam" is delusional thinking. The "Nature" is always bright and clear, without self, without people, without falling into numbers. But when there is "Conscious" then it falls into the list of numbers, falls into discrimination. "I" is also discrimination, also called the sixth consciousness. This consciousness is very cloudy in comparison. On the contrary, the seventh and eighth consciousnesses are a bit more pure. There are eight types of consciousness:

Eyes, nose, ears, tongue, body, mind are the first six consciousnesses, plus the seventh and eighth consciousnesses. Consciousness itself is not eight, but because it is a noun, it must be divided into eight. But generally speaking, it is just one, but there are eight different positions. Although there are eight different positions, they are still controlled by one dominant consciousness. Eight is one, one is eight. Eight doesn't mind one, one doesn't mind eight. From one is born eight, from eight gathered to become one, that is called consciousness.

"I" is our discriminating mind, which is the sixth consciousness. "The mind" not only discriminates but is full of delusions. The first six consciousnesses can be said to have a perceptual nature, because of the six senses that arise from the six senses. The six senses are: eyes, ears, nose, tongue, body, and mind; comes from seeing (vision), hearing (auditory), smelling (olfactory), tasting (taste), touching (tactile), understanding (perception). People create karma from those six senses, and their practice also comes from these six senses. If it is not influenced by external circumstances, it is practice. If you are turned around by the outside world, then you will fall.

noi_dung:
It's Heartbreaking for the Current Education System

Always follow the spirit of great public service and impartiality,

Brilliant brilliance, with a fearless spirit.

Today education in many countries is collapsing. However, there are still some people who strive hard to save the danger of moral decline. The actions of those who strive to strive compared to those who fall are like throwing a glass of water to extinguish a burning house. What is the reason why the education system collapsed like that? That's because people, the scholars in education, refuse to improve and don't know how to progress. Although they see students becoming more and more depraved, killing people, setting fires, robbing, and smoking drugs, they treat these things as nothing. They even publicly accused students of using drugs, having abortions, being unruly, secretly using birth control pills, etc. v... These bad behaviors only weaken students' will and destroy their conscience.

However, some educators still have a dedicated heart; exhort with all our might to save that damnation; For the sake of young people, rebuild good foundations. But the majority of educators have a dark mentality, promote lustful things, corrupt morals, and damage good morals, causing the aspirations of young people, heroes and talented people, to collapse and good roots to decline and be interrupted.

Before developing true wisdom, they learned all kinds of crazy things.

There are educators who even call for reforming people's minds. But those people are the enemies in the moral village. Because they use corrupt literature to cover up evil things; strongly oppose true education which is constructive education. They are like blind people bewitching the senseless. These things make people suffer and worry.

Those who serve in the education system must always follow the spirit of great public service, impartiality, brilliance, and fearless spirit to build a class of young people who know how to take control of the future. If so, we will not be ashamed of our conscience, nor ashamed to be a teacher to others. If you do not correct those mistakes, you are full of wrong knowledge, wrong views, wrong understandings, jealous obstacles, only want to seek fame and profit, push others down so that you can stand on top, always have false and deceitful behavior, then the education system will never be able to improve. Talented people will be lost, and the nation's future will also be very dangerous. Hopefully educators will shout for young people to pay attention. Always find a way to save the youth, so they don't have to fall into a deadlock and fall into ruin. If so, it is truly a blessing for the national society.
