tieu_de: Meditation requires an eye to choose the method
tom_tat: If you are not aware of the true method, you can go down an evil path
noi_dung:
Meditation requires an eye to choose the Dharma

If you are not aware of the true dharma, you can go down the wrong path.

People who study Buddha-dharma need to have Trach-phap-eye, that is, the eye that knows how to choose the Dharma; know which is Dharma and which is not Dharma; Which one is black, which one is white, which one is good, which one is evil. Remember not to mistake the fake for real, black for white, white for black, or take good for evil, evil for good. It's all crazy. When we want to perceive such Dharmas, we need to have eyes called Trach-dharma-eye.

First let go of the ego appearance. If there is an ego form, all kinds of obstacles will arise, and there will be no wisdom. Having the appearance of an ego gives rise to a selfish mind, which then gives birth to a mind of self-interest, a mind of pursuit, and a mind of greed. When you can't pray, and when you can't be greedy, then the mind of fighting is born, and you can win with the other person.

If there is no "ego," then what is called "ego"? Who is the ego? Who is this ego? You think about it and crave it. Like the question "Who is the Buddha's name?"The sentence "Who is the Buddha's name?" is greed, not for recitation. If we recite it over and over it is useless, we must be greedy for it. Greed is like using a chisel; Keep trying until you can pierce it, then you will be fully enlightened.

Momentarily unclear, momentarily greedy;

A time when there was no transparency, a time when the city was weak and greedy.

Meaning:

When you don't understand clearly, you need to consult.

Every time you don't understand clearly, you always need to consult.

Meditation is not just guessing, if we keep guessing that "Am I reciting Buddha's name? Do you recite Buddha's name? That person recites Buddha's name? Who recites Buddha's name?" Guessing again and again is not correct. I need to find "Ai." This word "Ai" is the Vajra-king Treasure Sword, which means the sword of wisdom. If you use this sword of wisdom to cut off all other delusions, wisdom will naturally appear.

If you do not realize or understand the method of meditation, but think that this method is the same as the method of reciting the Buddha's name, thinking that reciting as much as possible (instead of being greedy), that is extremely wrong. You don't need to chant a lot, just hold your breath for a long time, meditate a lot, any number of hours is fine. Even if you meditate for eighty thousand great kalpas without interruption, that is true meditation.

Why should we refer to the sentence "Who is Buddha's name?" This word "Ai" is also a lot of words. But because we are like monkeys, we always want to find this or that to do. Therefore, let us find the word "Ai", then our delusions will end. This means that using the word "Ai" is like using poison to treat poison. Meditating means clearing away dust (delusional thoughts). When we no longer have false thoughts, it is true that " is always awake." Meaning, always swept away. Why is it necessary to sweep dust? Because I don't want my mind to be filled with dust, I want to "sweep away all Dharmas, stay away from all appearances." That is the dharma-door of meditation.

If we don't have the eyes to choose the Dharma, if we don't understand the true Dharma, then we don't know what meditation is. If you don't know how to meditate, it's just a waste of practice. If you are not aware of the true dharma, you can go down the wrong path, so Trach-phap-eye, the eye that knows how to choose the dharma, is very important.

Whoever understands this zero can practice and attain fruition. All Dharmas arise through dependent conditions,

All Dharmas are destroyed by fate.

Buddha, Great Samana,

Often acts like a theory.

Meaning:

Dharmas arising from conditions,

Dhammas are destroyed by conditions.

The Great Samana Buddha,

Often said the same thing.

All Dharmas are created by causes and conditions, and then destroyed by causes and conditions. That is the principle of reincarnation, also the principle: "The ultimate opposite, the ultimate extreme." Meaning that when all things change to one extreme, they will turn around to reach the other extreme. When there is an extreme deadlock, there will be peace. That is the relative Dharma in this world.

Relative Dharma is like when good reaches the extreme and then turns into bad, when bad reaches the extreme, it turns into good. Just like when people are born, it is good, but when they die, it is bad and destructive. Birth, existence, difference, destruction; After being born, it will exist, after remaining, it will mutate, after mutating, it will be destroyed. Birth, old age, sickness, and death are all the same; When you are born, you will gradually grow old, when you get old you will get sick, when you get sick you will die. That is the dharma of cause and effect. Everyone lives, likes to live, and everyone must die, but is afraid of death. If we don't like living but also don't fear death, then that is a kind of concentration. Like people are often afraid of ghosts, but why are they afraid? Because demons are evil and cruel, they can harm and kill people. Therefore, people are afraid of ghosts, it is just a phenomenon of fear of death. If I'm not afraid of death, then I'm not afraid of anything. Whether it's ghosts, demons, or monsters, I'm not afraid; Nothing scares me at all. As for fear, there is still no concentration. When all fear is eliminated, then there is right concentration, right feeling, and only then can there be concentration. With concentration, a person will:

When faced with a wind knife, it's often frustrating,

Pretending so many poisons is leisurely.

Standing in front of the sword is still bold, Even if you force poison, it's still normal.

that if someone brought a knife to cut off my head, or used poison to kill me, I would not be afraid, my heart would not be disturbed. That's why? Because I have escaped birth and death "The reason for doing things, there is no afterlife." That means "finished what needed to be done, from now on there is no need to reincarnate." So it is said that if "a" is achieved, then everything is done.

But getting "a" is still not enough, we must make this "a" return to its origin: return to zero. Zero is a very magical principle, difficult to express. Whoever understands this zero can practice and attain fruition. How to understand this zero? First of all, you must understand number one. Because " is the best, everything is complete, " means that if you have one, all things are accomplished. This oneness is far from language, writing, from the mind's conditions, sweeping away all Dharma, far from all appearances. It is said again: "The one dharma is not established, all things are empty." Meaning there is no dharma established, everything is empty. If you want to reach this realm and morality, you must first reach "a,". Don't underestimate this number "a".

Heaven is the most pure,

The ultimate attainment of nirvana,

Humanity is the most holy.

Meaning:

It's okay "A" should be clear,

The land is "A" so it should be left alone,

The person who "A" became a Saint.

Why does the sky cover all things? It's because of God that I got this number "one". Why is the ground a support for all things? It's because the land has this number "one". If the land is lost, the land will collapse, icebergs, earthquakes, sea water will rise, and all kinds of disasters will arise. If any place loses this number of "one", then all kinds of disasters will arise in that place. If this number "one" is not lost, every place on earth will be safe.

"The most holy cause."If people truly reach this number "a", they can escape samsara, attain sainthood, and gain wisdom. Because people lose the number "one", they are stuck in samsara, revolving in the six paths, suffering all kinds of afflictions and ignorance. Eighty-four thousand troubles are born from the loss of this number "one". If you want to return to "a", you must first turn afflictions into Bodhi, turn birth and death into Nirvana; It's as easy as turning your hand, it's not that difficult! But why can't we turn the afflictions of birth and death into Bodhi Nirvana? Because I lost this number "one", and ran to number two, three, then ten, from ten to one hundred, then endlessly; Therefore, hundreds of thousands of millions of afflictions are born. Therefore, this number "a" is very important. However, because I lost this number "a", wanting to get it back is not easy. From the number "a", if you want to reverse it and return to zero, it is even more difficult.

I give you another simple example. When is it called "a"? Is there any time called "no?" For girls, from one to fourteen years old, for boys from one to twelve years old, during that period, the number "one has not yet been lost." When is the number "no?" From conception to birth, that is the period when you are in the number "no." At that time, all the afflictions Delusions, greed, anger, and ignorance are all absent. Until you know how to eat, hunger then gives birth to greed, anger, and stupidity begin to arise; But at this time, the number " has not yet been lost, " is the beginning of human life. From the number "not" turned into "one,", the number "one" is still a very complete number, because it is the beginning of everything. Until going through life's developments, other things will be added to this number "one", to turn into two, two into three, three into four, and so on, the more it increases, the greater the burden, and people become more foolish.

Nature means the number "emptiness," the number "emptiness" also means nature. "emptiness" nature means nothing at all, which is:

My origin is without one thing, who is this world?

Meaning:

In the past, there was nothing,

So why is there dust sticking to it?

Cultivation requires cultivating to the point of "ho venerable red child, " means the mind is like a child, the mind does not have anything. Like a child, that is, returning to old age. However, returning to old age is not saying that we should go drink milk, but it means that we no longer have greed, anger, ignorance, arrogance, and doubt. This is called the original return; no different from the views of a child, very sincere, no evil thoughts, no laziness, no greed for convenience, or greed for convenience. That is "Originally, there is no one thing, the land of this world is ".

To practice the Way, we need to clearly understand this principle to be truly enlightened. Why do I have to listen to sutra lectures? Because I want to return to my original form. Why do you want to practice? Also because we want to return to our original nature and restore all the turbulence in our mind. Don't use effort in the place of self, ego, and non-existence. If someone says something against my will, I feel uncomfortable and unhappy. Even touching a strand of hair makes me extremely painful and uncomfortable. If you even drop a drop of sweat to benefit the world, you won't do it. These are all extremely selfish spirits, unable to cultivate the Way.

People who practice the Way need to have no self, no cause, no Sentient Beings, no sentient beings (no self, no other, no Sentient Beings, no lifespan). Selflessness does not mean that we do not do things but ask others to do them for us. Inhumanity does not mean that when it's time to eat and drink, you say: "oh! Because I have no cause, I don't have anything to do with eating a little more, which means there is no one else." Even though at this moment I no longer have a human appearance (I don't see anyone else), other people still have that human appearance. When arguing or fighting, it becomes "without the form of Sentient Beings." Or when eating meat, it becomes "Without life and impersonation of the form." That is, the piece of meat does not have a life span. All are wrong interpretations. So what should be done?

What is the correct interpretation:

No Self (no self): That is, no self-centeredness, no calculation of benefits for oneself.

No Human Form (not seeing anyone): It means that we are not obstacles, we do not do things that are detrimental to others.

No Sentient Beings (not seeing Sentient Beings): It means considering all things to be the same as yourself.

Sentient Beings have the right to life, so we cannot take or kill any life, including humans and animals.

Therefore, when cultivating the Way, at any time, do not expect for yourself, do not calculate for yourself. Always think of others.

tieu_de: The Six Great Principles are the Five Precepts
tom_tat: When applying effort, you must know how to initiate, you must know how to let go, whatever you do, you must do it
noi_dung:
The Six Great Principles i.e. the Five Precepts

When applying effort, you must know how to initiate, you must know how to let go, whatever you do, you must do it.

People who like reciting Buddha's name will join the Buddha's room, people who like to meditate will join the Zen's room. People who do not like reciting the Buddha's name or do not like to meditate can join "the lazy house" or "the sleeping room." The lazy room or the sleeping room sounds strange but it actually makes a lot of sense.

"I'm lazy": Even if you're lazy, you can't be lazy. Even though you don't do anything, your mind always has something to do, which is idle thinking and delusion. Sometimes in heaven, sometimes on earth, sometimes as devils, sometimes in hell, sometimes as human, sometimes as heaven. It is in the mind that all kinds of machinery and materials are created in the six paths of reincarnation. Once this organ has been activated, moving back and forth, wanting to be lazy, is only a waste of energy and spirit. From then on, I became more and more tired, lazier, and felt like everything had no meaning and had no flavor at all.

What about "not sleeping well"? Sleeping but my mind is dreamy. Sometimes I dream of becoming rich, sometimes I dream of being poor and miserable, sometimes I dream of being an official, sometimes I dream of begging for food, sometimes I dream of seeing a tiger or a poisonous snake. Because of dreams, sleeping is not peaceful, even if you want to lose sleep, you cannot sleep.

Because I don't know how to apply effort, no matter what I do, it's not good. A person who knows how to use effort is good at doing anything, meditating or reciting Buddha's name are both good, even being lazy or sleeping, that person can also use effort.

The City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has five sects: Zen, Doctrine, Secret, Pure, and Vinaya. You can practice any method you want, feel free to choose, don't be shy. If you want to be lazy, you can sleep if you want. Because we are lazy and do not steal, that is maintaining the precepts. Even though we sleep and don't kill people or kill animals, that's still maintaining the precepts. Reciting the Buddha's name, meditating, or studying the Dharma, practicing the Vinaya, or practicing Tantra are all maintaining precepts. Therefore, when we study the five sects, we are observing the Five Precepts: Do not kill, do not steal, do not commit adultery, do not lie, and do not drink alcohol. Using effort means not breaking the precepts. Even though on the outside we don't appear to be practicing the precepts (other people don't see us practicing the precepts), in fact we practice without the appearance of practicing the precepts. We don't need to use the word maintaining precepts to visualize when we are keeping precepts; This way of using effort is very good.

For that reason, in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas you are free to choose your practice method, no one is controlling you. Because this country is a democratic country, Bodhimanda must practice democracy and individual freedom. So for the past many days, you can practice whatever dharma you want, just concentrate on practicing, do it right, do it well, pay attention and that's enough.

Furthermore, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has Six Great Teachings:

No Fighting: If there is no fighting, it will not lead to killing. Killing is caused by the evil mind of fighting. When competing, we just want ourselves to win and the other person to lose, even if it means countless deaths.

No Greed: If you are not greedy, you will not steal. Why steal other people's things? It's because I have a greedy mind. If you don't have a greedy mind, if someone gives you something, you won't take it. If you eliminate greed, you will definitely not commit the crime of stealing.

No Pursuit: Without pursuit, lustful thoughts will not arise. Lust is due to one's desire. A girl wants a boy, a boy wants a girlfriend, it's all about pursuing the other person. Not only asking but also pursuing and pursuing, like a drill, just aim forward and drill. If there is no desire, how can there be the idea of ​​adultery? A handsome boy and a pretty girl are just two pieces of stinky meat. Why greed? If we don't have any desire, then we can't commit this sexual precept.

Not being selfish: Not being selfish will help you not lie. People lie because they are afraid of losing their own interests, so their selfish mind acts mischievously. Then I deceive others, tell lies, and don't want others to know my true face.

No Self-Interest: No self-interest will help you not violate the alcohol precepts. Why do people drink alcohol? It's because I want to enjoy it, I want my body to be happy. But happiness makes my mind confused and confused; I thought I had become a fairy, floating in the sky. When you are drunk, you curse others and do whatever you want, increasing your lust. Some people want to bring wine to help their blood circulate and feel refreshed. But after drinking it, everything is forgotten. It's the same thing as smoking opium, drugs, and drugs. This is all caused by the mind of self-interest; That's why I went out to drink.

No Echo:

Thus, the Six Great Tongs are the Five Precepts. Why not say the Five Precepts? That's because the word Five-Precepts sounds familiar, so when hearing about don't kill, don't steal, don't commit adultery, don't lie, don't drink alcohol, people often say: "I know, why do you keep saying this?" Therefore, it should be changed to: don't fight, don't be greedy, don't seek, don't be selfish, don't seek personal gain, and don't lie. Everyone has heard these nouns and already knows them. But very few people actually practice them, so I repeat:

Not fighting means not killing;

Not being greedy means not stealing;

Not seeking means not being lustful;

Not being selfish means not lying;

Don't take advantage of yourself, that is, don't drink alcohol.

tieu_de: Expression of Virtue
tom_tat: When starting to practice, people who study Buddhism must sow seeds in the ground. After a seed is sown, can it sprout and grow? See if the predestined relationship is enough or not. Seeds grow smoothly when all supporting conditions are full...
noi_dung:
Expression of Virtue

Cultivation means cultivating true morality,

don't block anyone, don't be afraid of anyone blocking you.

When starting to practice, people who study Buddhism must sow seeds in the ground. After a seed is sown, can it sprout and grow? See if the predestined relationship is enough or not. Seeds flourish when all supporting conditions are complete. If not enough, the seeds can be destroyed. If we consider that when we develop Bodhi mind and plant the seed of Bodhi, let's see if that seed can be planted deep or not, is it very solid?

If we plant deeply enough and firmly enough, then in the future the seeds will grow roots. If you want to achieve Bodhi results, it takes an equivalent amount of time. Let's see how we can use our efforts? If we work hard to advance, attain enlightenment, attain enlightenment, then we can consider it as achieving success.

From the time the seeds give birth to the roots until they bloom and bear fruit; That process takes a long time and requires constant nourishment, watering, and fertilization. What is fertilizer? That is, morality. Practitioners in any place must rely on morality, taking morality as the basis of precepts.

Confucianism says:

"Virtue is the original, fake talent is the end." Meaning that virtue is the root and material wealth is the tip. Virtue is the root of man, and material wealth is the bottom line. People cultivating the Tao must always know how to regret blessings and should not waste money and material things. In this way, over a long period of time, you can cultivate your virtue. Fruits are produced very quickly. If you don't try your best to water and fertilize, the fruit will easily wither and die. Therefore, for practitioners, the most important thing is to pay attention to virtue.

Virtue is gathered in very small places: "The little good things are undoing" means don't consider the small good things without doing them, then just wait to do the big good things. There are not many great good things. Big mountains are made up of small particles of dust. Even though the dust is small, if there is a lot of it, it becomes a big mountain. Although virtue is small, if we accumulate a lot of virtue, it can become a large mass of virtue.

Not going against morality is virtue. Not hindering others means being virtuous. No matter what you do, you should consider it your duty to help others. In terms of benefits, time, culture or wisdom, or everything, if we hinder others and do not benefit anyone, we have gone against morality. Therefore, in every move, in every word, in every conduct, we must not go against basic morality. If you want to practice religion, you first need to cultivate morality. Without virtue, you cannot practice religion. There is a person who wants to practice the Way and demons come to find him, because this person has no virtue. So say:

Fake virtue is wild, fake talent is wild.

Meaning:

Morality is the root, money is the top.

Morality is like the sun and moon, like heaven and earth, and like human life. Without morality, we have no life, no sun, no moon, and no heaven and earth. What is morality? That is, taking the benefit of others as the main priority, not hindering others as the Principles, and in the heart is full of Humanity, Righteousness, Respect, Wisdom, and Faith.

Humanity: A compassionate mind that does not want to kill the lives of others.

Meaning: The conscious mind knows to do what is right, and to do it very properly, in line with the middle path, without excesses or shortcomings, neither leaning to the right nor deviating to the left, always the middle path. If you understand the meaning, you will not steal. A virtuous person never steals other people's things.

Ceremony: It is the second ceremony of formalities and rituals. If we are polite, we will not commit adultery. Stealing and adultery are both impolite and contrary to morality.

Wisdom: People with wisdom never drink alcohol, smoke cigarettes, drugs, or poisons. Stupid people do these crazy things.

Faithful: People who are faithful never lie.

Humanity, Righteousness, Respect, Wisdom, Faith, these are called the Five Permanences. As long as we have all of these Five Permanences, we have morality and virtue. Therefore, morality is born from the mind. But when emitted, it has many forms: blue, yellow, red, white, and black. That is the expression of virtue, the light of virtue. Therefore, Mr. Han Du in the article Nguyen Dao has a passage that says: "Charity is the virtue of humanity. Humanity and doubt are the meaning. Because of this child, peace comes from the Way. Self-esteem and self-reliance have nothing but virtue." Meaning charity, humanity. Kindness in the right way (reasonable) is called Righteousness. Thanks to that, progress is called the Way. Having enough self-sufficiency and not relying on the outside should be called Virtue." Mr. Mencius also said: "Humanity and propriety are rooted in the mind, natural beauty is born, natural views are present, light is the foundation, kindness is fourfold, four elements are speechless." Meaning Humanity, Righteousness, Rites, and Wisdom are rooted in one's mind. Its color shines on the face, shines on the back, and uses the limbs. The four bodies don't need to be said, but the expression is clear. A person with virtue not only shows it on his face, but also shows the light of virtue on his back, even his hands and feet can express that virtue. This characteristic does not need to be said, it is discovered by itself, allowing everyone to see clearly. The manifestation of true virtue is through diligence. This virtue cannot be disguised. If it is false, it is only temporary, and cannot permanently deceive others.

Cultivating the Way means cultivating true morality, not hindering others, nor being afraid of others hindering you. Whoever hinders me, I accept it. "If things go against your will, you can accept them as you please. Anyone who is not compassionate or unreasonable to you is your good-knowledge. If we can "reverse the future and smooth life", then we can see our patience and patience. Don't let other people's words touch your mind. There are people who act like "is motionless" because they don't know shame, that's not right. We must practice " immobility, " means to endure things that other people cannot endure. That's what we call true practice, otherwise we have to practice from the beginning.

In Taoism, it is said: "Three flowers gather on top, five qi trieu Nguyen," means the manifestation of perfect morality. Those who believe in Buddhism hear this term and think they are pagans. In fact, what is called paganism? What is internal religion? There is nothing foreign or internal about this name. That is only used to visualize the results of practice. "Tam Hoa" means essence, energy, spirit, these three things have transformed into a kind of light. "The Five Qis" means Humanity, Righteousness, Rites, Wisdom, and Trust. These five energies are completely perfect, so they are called the Five Qi Yuan Qi.

In Buddhism, when morality is perfected, one will achieve Great Wisdom, Equal Nature Wisdom, Wonderful Contemplation Wisdom, and Accomplished Wisdom. That means Tam

The body, the Four Wisdoms, the Five Eyes, and the Six Intelligences are not lacking in anything. (Three Bodies: dharmakaya, sambhogakaya, incarnation; Four Wisdoms: Great Perfection of Scenery, Equality of Nature Wisdom, Wonderful Observation Wisdom, Accomplished Wisdom; Five Eyes: Buddha Eye, Dharma Eye, Wisdom Eye, Heavenly Eye, Flesh Eye; Six Insights: Heavenly Eye, Heavenly Ear, Other Minds, Divine, Full of Life, Fully Accessed.) Missing one thing means not reaching the realm of perfection. Therefore, Buddhism has all solemn virtues and can cover all religions, and all religions are only a part of Buddhism. That's why I often say: "Buddhism is like a university, Taoism and other advanced religions are considered high school, worldly religions like Confucianism are only at the elementary level."

In elementary school, high school or university, everyone is a student; In the world of religions, believers are religious figures. Therefore, we cannot classify, separate, and consider our own religion as good and other religions as bad: "Entering as a slave, leaving as an o chi" means that if you follow, you belong to your side, if you don't follow, you will be criticized, that attitude is wrong. All religions are a part of Buddhism. This point of view is correct. Because the Buddha said: "All Sentient Beings have the wisdom of Tathagata and can become Buddhas." All Sentient Beings have Buddha nature. So pagans are also Sentient Beings and have the opportunity to become Buddhas, so how can we leave pagans outside of Buddhism? The scope of Buddhism covers all of space, transforms the dharma realm, has no boundaries, no barriers to separate, no self and no other. Therefore, people who study Buddhism must have a generous mind and not be too narrow-minded.

In Taoism, virtuous people have an expression that others can tell by looking at them, such as white hair like a crane, and a face that is extremely rosy, lush, and youthful. That's why? It is because their morality is influenced by changes. Even though they have white hair, their hair is not dry and has a very clear air, a strand of their hair can radiate light. People who are diligent and have opened their five eyes will know immediately when they see it.

Buddhism is one level higher because not only the hair radiates light, but the whole body, every hair pore, radiates light. Every pore of theirs is different from ordinary people. People who practice diligently in Buddhism can turn white hair into black, and teeth fall out and grow back. There are also people in Taoism who regrow lost teeth, but they cannot do it for the whole body, each pore radiates light, that is the difference with Buddhism. Do you want to consider whether this person is a wise person or not? There is no need to have five eyes, as long as we practice, we will see and know if that person is a wise person or not? Is that person virtuous? People without virtue have disgusting and ugly faces that make everyone afraid and stay away.

tieu_de: Meditation Hall Hoi Ngu
tom_tat: Experienced practitioners want to save life and escape death, so they hold on to the first line earnestly, not for a second or a minute that they do not use it.
noi_dung:

But these are good roots that are possessed of defilement (being possessed of defilements means having afflictions), so it is said: "The race of possessing the defilements of origin, reincarnation is difficult to break." Whenever the origin of the defilements is planted, it is difficult to end samsara. We must practice the cause of the world to escape samsara.

(VI) Asura's Dharma Realm

Tula is violent,

Blessed and powerless,

Bravely fighting,

Phu karma shield.

Meaning:

Tula has a violent nature.

Blessed, but not powerful.

Likes to fight.

Floating and sinking as karma leads.

A-tu-la is a Sanskrit word translated as unrighteousness. Immorality is ugly. Male Asura has an extremely ugly appearance and likes to fight with others. The female A-tu-la has an extremely beautiful appearance and loves to fight with emotions, that is, using jealousy, jealousy, obstacles, ignorance, and afflictions.

Although these Sentient Beings form a Dharma world, no matter where in the six paths, there are Sentient Beings who like to fight, are extremely hot-tempered and fierce, and only like to command others and not be commanded by others; Just liking to rule others but not liking to be controlled by anyone, those are all manifestations of Asura. Asuras among humans are divided into evil and good. Good Asuras are the army and generals in the country. Asuras are robbers, thieves, people who like to fight and kill others.

Asuras in heaven like to fight with heavenly soldiers and heavenly generals. All day long they were only thinking about how to attack De Thich in order to rob the throne and take the throne to become De Thich. However, even though they fought all the time, they always lost. Why? Because although they are in heaven enjoying blessings, they have no power. Therefore, even though we fought against heavenly soldiers and heavenly generals, we still failed in the end.

Among the animals there are also Asuras. They like to oppress their fellow creatures or other animals, such as wolves, tigers, lions... who like to eat other animals because they have an A-tu-la nature. Snakes or eagles are also A-tu-la things.

Asuras among demons like to bully other demons. Demons also have good and evil types. Demons don't care about right or wrong. Since ancient times, demons have never known right from wrong, but demons are even more ignorant of right from wrong.

Asura's violent nature: Asura's personality is very brutal. Blessed with no power:

They have the blessings of the gods, but do not have the same power as the gods.

Therefore, they want to compete for rights, but cannot win.

Look at the world today: A world of Asura. Everywhere there is talk of struggle and struggle. Fight for this, fight for that. You knock me down, I push you down.

Karma shield: Depending on which direction karma leads them to go, they will follow that path. Therefore, practitioners must avoid fighting and arguing with others. Don't be eager to win or like to argue. You should not have a violent and fierce personality. Then we can escape the Asuras.

In short, Asura never talked about right or wrong. No matter who they are with, they often get angry. To be clear, among the nine Dharma Realms of Sentient Beings, Asura is present in the five Dharma Realms. Among animals, birds and animals also have A-tu-la. Crocodiles are a type of Asura in water. Horses also have A-tu-la: if this thing is in a herd of horses, they cause a lot of trouble, so they are called "Harmful group of horses,"horses that disrupt the herd. Cows also have that A-tu-la; This cow is the A-tu-la nature. As for the dogs, they are indeed the Asuras. Therefore, dog owners and people who are often close to dogs can be infected with that A-tu-la nature. Therefore be careful. Don't run after the Asuras!

(VII) Dharma-realm of Humanity

Humanity and harmony,

The crime of adultery.

Virtue rises and falls,

May you rest in peace!

Meaning:

Harmony is the human way,

Merit and sin are mixed together

Virtue rises and falls

Who else did it!

In the human world, there are good and evil people. Human nature is inherently peaceful and can be in harmony with others, so I say harmony is humane. Mutual sin: meaning that humans are not completely good or completely evil. If he had been completely good, he would have gone to heaven, but if he had been completely evil, he would have definitely become an animal, a hungry ghost, or fallen into hell. Therefore, every time people do a little work, they commit a little crime. Sometimes the merits are many, the sins are few; Or many sins, little merit. When you have many merits and few sins, you will be born into a wealthy family. If we have little merit and many sins, we will be born into a poor and miserable family. Between these two extremes (merit and sin) there are thousands of differences, depending on the degree of evil karma created. Humans are neither yin nor yang. Because pure yin will make people turn into demons, pure yang will make all humans ascend to heaven, there will be nothing human left!

Virtue rises and falls: If you do good deeds or merit, you will rise. If you commit harsh crimes, you will fall into hell. Revel in peace: no one can force you to fall into hell, or become a hungry ghost, or turn into an animal. It's all created by you. That: "I do it, I bear it." I do it myself, I have to bear the consequences. That is the human realm.

(VIII) Dharma-realm Animals

Animals are greedy,

Many children have no cover,

The combination of black and white

Thi and phi are discussed.

Meaning:

Greedy animals,

A lot but not boring.

Take black to make white

Not sure right or wrong.

The seven Dharma-realms mentioned above are all good Dharma-realms, you can try it, go there and act out. There are only three remaining Dharma Realms, you cannot try to know. Because if you fall into these three paths, it will be difficult to escape. Therefore: "If a person's body is lost, it will be difficult to recover in ten thousand lifetimes." (If a human body is lost, it will be difficult to recover in ten thousand lifetimes). Therefore it is very dangerous.

In the current animal world, there is not only one type. Animals have hundreds of thousands of millions of different things. Just talking about flying species, there are hundreds of thousands of species. There are not many species that can run, from things as small as mice, as large as elephants, or large animals like deer, bears, horses, goats...

There are hundreds of thousands of species of things on earth. There are hundreds of thousands of aquatic species, including seals, walruses, etc. Whether you are a physicist, a chemist, a biologist, a zoologist, a doctor or an expert, it is impossible to know all of these things.

Where do those animals come from? Only comes from "tham". "Animals are greedy": no matter what it is, they want a lot, a little is not enough. Because they are " without many threats, " has many but is not boring. So what is black, they do not realize that it is black. They think: "A! This is white!" Therefore: "As black equals white." Recognizing what is black is what is white; what is bad is considered good. That is the sign that they have no reason at all. So they are greedy for anything, even dirty things like dog poop. The more they eat it, the more delicious and fragrant it becomes. "Dispute in the world" means they do not know what is right and what is wrong; Can't distinguish between right and wrong, can't understand everything clearly because there's no reason anymore. When they are greedy, they become confused. So we are covered by ignorance, we don't know anything.

Therefore, if humans like us are greedy, it is very dangerous; Too much greed can easily lead to turning into animals. Hey buddy! Any monastic who does not practice according to Buddha's precepts will fall into hell a little sooner. That's why the ancients had the saying: "The gate of hell was before the monks were" (meaning, at the gate of hell, there are many monks and Taoists). They stood waiting at the gates of hell. Taoists or monks think that hell is a fun place, but when they get there they realize that it is not fun at all!

(IX) Dharma-realm of hungry ghosts

Demons of joy and anger

I'm so confused

Crazy ignorance,

The darkest days and moons.

Meaning:

Demons like to be angry,

Confusion Cause and Effect

Ignorance is crazy

The days pile up.

Most people know ghosts. Some people believe that ghosts exist, but others say that ghosts do not exist. Even many Buddhists do not believe in ghosts. What is a devil? Demons are a kind of negative energy, having a shadow but no form, or having a form but no shadow. Many times you see a dark shadow, but when you look closely, the shadow disappears. Or sometimes you see a shadow that looks like a person, but in the blink of an eye it disappears. It is difficult to clearly determine the truth about this.

How many demons are there? As much as the sand in the Ganges River. If you want to know clearly how many types of ghosts there are, you should practice the Way. When you can cultivate the Five Eyes and Six Insights, you will clearly know how many types of demons there are.

Someone said: "There are no ghosts!" I told him that if there were no ghosts, there would be no Buddha, no humans, and no animals. Because animals, humans, and Asuras all transformed from demons. Even gods, Arhats, Pratyekabuddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Buddhas all advance from the devil path. Why? Because the ten Dharma realms do not leave a single thought in the mind. This one thought creates the ten Dharma realms. If you do devilish things, you will fall into the devil's path. If you do human work, you will go to the human world; if you do asura work, you will go to the asura world. If you do the work of an Arhat, you will become an Arhat. If you do the things of the Pratyekabuddha, you will reach the Pratyekabuddha. If you do the work of a Bodhisattva, you will become a relative of Bodhisattvas. If you do Buddha's work, you will become a Buddha. If you do hellish things, you will fall into hell. Therefore one thought in the present creates everything.

"Ghosts of joy and anger" As demons, they love to get angry and angry. Treat them well, and they will also be angry; If you treat them poorly, they will become even angrier. What interests them the most?

That means creating trouble for others. You treat them properly, they also cause you trouble. If you don't treat them nicely, they will also cause trouble.

Hence the saying: "Burning incense invites demons."Even though you light incense out of respect for them, they come to cause trouble for you and make you sick. Therefore, Confucius said: "Respect ghosts and spirits, far away." This means we must respect ghosts and spirits, but we should not be close to them, so we should be a little distant.

I am so confused about the cause: They do not understand the retribution; But the cause is also unknown. Therefore they do not know good or bad. In the past, whenever we planted good causes, we reaped good results; If you plant good causes, you will reap good results; if you plant bad causes, you will reap evil results. Planting melons, harvesting melons; plant beans, get beans. But the demons do not understand this principle of Cause and Effect. Therefore, they plant eggplants but hope to reap chili peppers, plant chili peppers but hope to reap cucumbers; Completely confused and confused, it should be said to be a confused person.

They "Ignorance is crazy, day and night are deep": accumulating more and more ignorance every day. The more karma you create, the more serious your sin; The more serious the crime, the more karma it creates. Therefore, he fell into the path of demons.

Dharma-realm of hell

Hell of suffering

No door self-transmission

Start or create karma

Life is cyclical.

Mean:

Hell is full of suffering

No door but come in

Start or create karma

Suffer cyclic retribution.

Hell is a place of extreme suffering. If you want to travel to hell, I guarantee you will go there immediately. How? There is a saying:

"Whenever you are sad, you are walking around in hell. Laugh happily and old people become young. Crying all the time, creating a dark room in the underworld"

Sadness and sorrow are the cause of hell. If you laugh happily, that is the cause of heaven. That:

Since ancient times, gods have no distinction,

Only joy arises, not sadness.

Mean:

Since ancient times, fairies have not performed miracles,

Only be born happily, without worries.

If you often laugh and smile, then even if you are old, you are still young. Crying is a very troublesome thing. Hell of sorrow and suffering: This means that there is no joy or peace in hell, only sorrow and suffering. "No gate self-piercing"; This means that hell has never had a door. The door to hell is placed and opened by ourselves. I just keep digging in, (like an awl keeps drilling in) and if I can't get in, I just keep trying to get in. "Start or create karma." Why fall into hell? It's because we are ignorant, ignorant, and therefore create negative karma. No matter what career you practice, you will receive that reward, not one bit wrong. This is a non-stop cycle. It should be said: "Circular retribution."

The ten precepts are one-minded

Never let go of thoughts

sensory ability to test thoughts

Set up a post on the bank.

Meaning:

Ten Dharma Realms, one mind,

Not beyond the present thought,

Realizing this thought,

Immediately get to the other shore.

The four Holy Dharma Realms are Buddha, Bodhisattva, Sravaka, Pratyekabuddha and the six ordinary Dharma Realms are heaven, human, Asura, hungry ghost, animal, hell, a total of ten Dharma Realms. Where do the Ten Dharma Realms come from? From an idea in my current mind. Therefore: "The ten precepts are one-minded, without abandoning thoughts.

The ability to test the concept: If you clearly understand the current concept, you will immediately reach the other shore: immediately to the other shore, that is, Maha Prajnaparamita. What is the other shore? It is enlightenment, no longer confused; destroy ignorance. When ignorance is destroyed, the dharmakaya will appear.

tieu_de: What does it take to enjoy life? Leaving Home
tom_tat: Monastics must have a solid foundation for practice. What is a strong foundation? That means strictly following the precepts. Monastics must learn by heart the "Four Commentaries" i.e. the novice law, the monk law, the law...
noi_dung:
What is the need to become a monk to enjoy life?

Don't intentionally lie, don't do things like "cover your ears and steal the bell."

Monastics must have a solid foundation for practice. What is a strong foundation? That means strictly following the precepts. A monastic person must learn by heart "The Fourfold Commentary", i.e. the Novice Discipline, the Bhikkhu Discipline, the Bhikkhuni Discipline, the Brahma Vong Sutra, etc. and then study it thoroughly, to be qualified to become a monk.

If the foundation is not solid, thinking about money all day and thinking about lust, then " may become a monk in body, but his mind will not enter the Dharma." Like that, he is hundreds of thousands of miles away from the Dharma. These monastics do corrupt things in Buddhism, they cannot be recognized as monastics.

A monastic person is not allowed to go to this fate or another, nor can he go alone to a small temple and call Lay Buddhist to protect the dharma. Accepting offerings alone, such behavior is not in accordance with the rules established by the Buddha. If we have these behaviors, we must quickly change them, because:

Donor one lak rice, heavy and weak Tu Di Son.

Eat the willow without cultivating the Way, and eat the willow with the enlightenment.

Meaning:

The grain of rice the donor gave was as heavy as Mount Meru.

After eating, he does not cultivate the Way, wears horns and feathers.

In ancient times, people who truly practiced Buddhism lived in thatched houses, plowed their own fields, and ate their own food; Absolutely not thanks to external conditions. For the purpose of eliminating greed, they live in thatched houses and practice. Or maybe they go into seclusion because they want to make sure their education and morality are strong. If you truly practice the Way, you can live alone, but you cannot receive Lay Buddhist offerings alone. To do so is to turn the Right Dharma into the End of Dharma, and it is also to destroy Buddhism.

Currently, practitioners prefer to practice alone in monasteries. Why so? Because if they don't keep the precepts, no one will see them. If they break the rules, no one will know. They can do whatever they want and do whatever they want, no one is controlling them, they are free, it can be said that there are no constraints at all. Or maybe someone else gathers a number of Lay Buddhists in their monastery and says they're doing this and that, but in reality they're just borrowing Buddha's clothes and relying on the Buddha's name to make a living.

There are monastics who do not use Lay Buddhist offerings for Buddhist activities, but instead use that money to buy luxury items, cars, and do things for personal benefits. Or maybe you buy a T.V., then watch T.V. every day, forgetting to chant the sutras morning and night. Or buy a refrigerator to store delicious and strange foods. In short, they are addicted to enjoyment, greedy for things, greedy for happiness. The current atmosphere is exactly like that. They completely transformed the ascetic nature of Buddhism, truly betraying the suffering of Shakyamuni Buddha in the past!

Someone said: "Born in this era, you need to watch T.V., you need to know international news, otherwise you're blind, deaf and dumb and don't know anything." What if you know about real life things? Knowing what happens in real life, can death be avoided?

Some people say: "Can people who practice avoid death?" You practice, when you die, you have to die, but before you die, your mind is clear, absolutely no worries, no confusion, and you die peacefully. If we don't practice, when we die we will die; But he died confused, confused, and confused. Not remembering the south or the north, the heart is not pure, holding on to hatred and dying. That's the difference, do you know?

For true practitioners, when they die, their mind is very clear, knowing where they came from and where they will go; There is clearly no ambiguity at all, and we have not forgotten our original appearance. People who don't practice are confused when they arrive, and when they leave they are even more confused, spending their whole life confused. They don't know why they came or why they left. I don't know where it came from or where it went. Completely in the dark.

The purpose of becoming a monk is to escape life and death, not for enjoyment. So once you become a monk, why do you need to be greedy for material enjoyment? If you have the greed for enjoyment, why do you need to become a monk? I advocate that no matter who wants to stay alone in a small temple to find ways to enjoy themselves, it is better to return to the secular world. Why? Because becoming a layman is much better than staying alone in a small temple, it does not create the karma just mentioned. I hope the public will pay attention to that point.

Saying that a solitary practitioner resides in a small pagoda for the purpose of not cultivating but to enjoy offerings, there are definitely many people who do not want to hear that statement. I don't care whether you want to listen or not, I still speak because I think about the future of Buddhism. So if you say something, it will make others uncomfortable. One more time: "Anyone who is a monk likes to enjoy himself, without practice, he is just masquerading as a monk." I hope that fellow monks encourage each other, remind each other, don't intentionally lie, don't do things like "Stealing bells by covering your ears." Cover your saint's eyes with cheesecloth.

Lecture November 11, 1983

tieu_de: People Leaving Home Must Recite Three Sutras
tom_tat: What are those three sutras? These are the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Shurangama Sutra, and the Lotus Sutra. These three sutras were spoken by Buddha Shakyamuni, narrated by Venerable Ananda, then written on leaves and passed down in...
noi_dung:
Monks Must Recite Three Sutras

If you understand the realm of these three sutras, then you will not be in vain becoming a Buddhist.

What are those three sutras? These are the Avatamsaka Sutra, the Shurangama Sutra, and the Lotus Sutra. These three sutras were spoken by Shakyamuni Buddha, narrated by Venerable Ananda, then written on leaves and circulated in the world, becoming the sutras that Buddhists must learn and recite.

Monastics and lay people in the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas must learn to recite these three sutras. At least memorize the Shurangama Sutra, or two or three volumes, that is the ideal. If we are to explain the meaning of sutras, we cannot just rely on the words. If we do not seek profound understanding, it is of no use. If you can understand the realm of these three sutras, then you will not be in vain as a Buddhist follower.

When Buddha was thirty years old, he sat under the Bodhi tree and attained enlightenment. During the twenty-one days of meditating, he preached the Avatamsaka Mahayana Sutra for the Dharmakaya Great Master; This sutra covers the twelve volumes of the Tripitaka, clearly explaining the unobstructed realm of all things in this universe, which can also be called "The realm of the one true Dharma-realm."

When the Buddha was sixty-two years old, Venerable A-Nan paid too much attention to education and literature, and neglected intellectual practice. Unfortunately, the Venerable Ma Dang Gia's daughter used Brahma's mantra to do him a disservice, almost breaking the precepts. The Buddha had to use the Shurangama Mantra to save Ananda from the female tribulation, then preach the Shurangama Buddha Sutra to Ananda. This sutra is a sutra that opens wisdom and demonstrates morality. If we develop the truth in the sutras, our wisdom will definitely be as vast and vast as the ocean.

When the Buddha was seventy-two years old, he was on Linh Son mountain in the Dharma Flower Assembly, for the great Arhats and great Bodhisattvas, preaching the principle "A Buddha Vehicle", also the principle of how to become a Buddha. At that time, because those who followed the Hinayana dharma abandoned their narrow-mindedness and changed it to a broad-mindedness, and were prophesied by the Buddhas to become Buddhas in the future, the Lotus Sutra of the Wonderful Dharma was considered the Sutra that teaches Buddhahood.

If practitioners imitate students and diligently read books with all their heart, then the Tripitaka and twelve sutras will be easy to memorize. But after becoming a monk, there are people who think that they are complete, that reciting the Buddha's name, meditating, studying the teachings, maintaining precepts, and reciting mantras are enough, so they do not study the sutras, because they underestimate the importance of studying the sutras. So the next generation is not as good as the previous generation; create a habit of laziness. That is the misfortune of Buddhism. If we do not promptly correct that misconception, then the future of Buddhism will not know where it will go.

Lecture November 12, 1983

Four Great Bodhisattvas came to the West to propagate Buddhism and help Buddhism flourish.

In China there are four Bodhimandas:

Wutai Mountain in Son Tay province is the Bodhimanda of Bodhisattva Manjushri.

Emei Mountain in Sichuan Province is the Bodhimanda of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.

Cuu Hoa Mountain in An Hoi province is the Bodhimanda of Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva.

The Holy City of Ten Thousand Buddhas is the Bodhimanda of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva, worshiping Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva as the master and Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva as the subordinate.

Every person who believes in Buddhism can eliminate greed, anger, and ignorance (the three poisons). Without greed, without anger, without ignorance, the mind will be clear, the world will be peaceful, there will be no more war forever.

Those who want to worship Bodhisattva Manjushri are invited to come to Vancouver. If you want to worship Bodhisattva Samantabhadra, please come to Seattle. If you want to worship Avalokiteshvara Bodhisattva, please come to the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas. If you want to worship Ksitigarbha Bodhisattva, you should go to Los Angeles. tieu_de: Leaving Home is the Story of a Great Man
tom_tat: A great man is someone who has the spirit of patience and does not give up, overcoming all difficulties
noi_dung:
Renunciation is the Story of a Great Man

A great man is someone who has the spirit of patience and does not give up, overcoming all hardships.

In life, becoming a monk is a very rare thing, and it is also a difficult thing for people to understand. Why do we have to suffer when becoming a monk? Because when you become a monk, you are no longer allowed to have sex between men and women, you are not allowed to dance, and you are also not allowed to eat, drink or drink. If you want to become an outstanding and talented person, you must endure what others cannot endure, must accept suffering that others cannot endure. Only by cultivating like this can one become an indestructible diamond body. So say:

Unconscious for a moment, the bones are cold,

Cham dac apricot flower with fragrant flowers?

Meaning:

Not once was it bone-chillingly cold,

Why do apricot blossoms bloom so fragrant?

People who become monks need to prepare their hearts and minds: Renunciation is because they want to escape birth and death; I want to forever be free from the suffering of samsara. Even when facing all kinds of hardships, don't be afraid. The more suffering, the better. When encountering suffering, don't give up, change your original intention, and find a way to turn back. We need to have the spirit of patience, not to give up, to overcome all suffering and hardships, that is what a great man is. Therefore, becoming a monk is not something that everyone can do, even a general may not be able to do it. Therefore it is said: "Renunciation is a matter of the gods, " is not a matter of flies, mosquitoes and small fry. There is a saying:

Feeling suffering means suffering, enjoying blessings means eliminating blessings.

Meaning:

Only by suffering will suffering end, enjoying blessings will eliminate blessings.

You consider that the great and virtuous monks of ancient times all attained enlightenment through ascetic practice. None of the Patriarchs attained enlightenment due to the enjoyment of happiness. You searched all over the Tripitaka and couldn't find anyone.

We need to have patience in order to benefit from the fullness of Dharma joy. You must have an austere mind to attain enlightenment. Cannot go against Buddhism. We must always focus our minds on effort, bring our thoughts back, without any wandering thoughts, that is to control "mind like a horse, mind like a monkey." Don't let your mind run after external circumstances.

When becoming a monk to practice the Way, you must first eliminate greed, destroy anger, and eliminate delusion. Eliminate those three poisons and wisdom will naturally appear.

How can we completely wipe out those things? That is, using Precepts, Concentration, and Hue (the three teachings) as tools. Precepts cure greed, Concentration cures anger, wisdom cures ignorance. Therefore, people who become monks are called "Sa-Mon." Sa-Mon is translated as "Necessary, " means "Need to practice Precepts, Concentration, Hue, which means eliminating greed, anger, and ignorance." That means diligently keeping Precepts, Concentration, Hue, eliminating greed, anger, and ignorance. If everyone were free from greed, anger and ignorance, the world would be peaceful.

Lecture November 18, 1983

tieu_de: Buddha Nature Is the Origin of All Sentient Beings
tom_tat: In the beginning, when the universe was vast and began to open up, there were no people, no Sentient Beings, no world, basically nothing. But slowly towards the end of life, there began to be Sentient Beings. Let's ask Sentient Beings…
noi_dung:
Buddha Nature Is the Origin of All Sentient Beings

In the beginning, when the universe was vast and began to open up, there were no people, no Sentient Beings, no world, basically nothing. But slowly towards the end of life, there began to be Sentient Beings. Where do Sentient Beings come from? Some people say it came from where monkeys evolved. But where did monkeys evolve? If apes evolved into humans, why aren't we seeing apes continue to transform into humans now? This is nothing but the doctrine of unintelligent people. If so, why don't they say that humans can be transformed from mice, or that furry animals can evolve! How could they know that the rat wasn't human? All kinds of flying, jumping, wading underwater, animals, plants; to the winged creatures of heaven; In the sea, fish, crabs, shrimps, frogs and humans have vitality; or herbs. Where did the ancestors of all concubines, arrows, caves, and food come from? Everything flows from Buddha nature.

In heaven and earth, heaven and earth have the characteristic of being constantly born and transformed, infinitely transformed; constantly regenerate. Because there is Buddha nature, without Buddha nature everything is destroyed, only Buddha nature can go through hundreds of thousands of years without being destroyed, always lasting. Because of Buddha nature, there is a transformation into the ten Dharma Realms. These ten Dharma realms are no more than the mind's mindfulness, this mind's mindfulness is Dharma nature, also another name for Buddha nature; Therefore, humans are transformed by Buddha nature, and animals are transformed by fallen humans. In these ten dharma realms, we can see clearly. Stupid people think that human ancestors are monkeys, Muslims say that ancestors are pigs, Indians say cows are gods; that is boundary view; Knowing only a little bit without knowing the whole thoroughly makes the world become enchanting. Those people also wrote books establishing theories, some said it was science, some said it was philosophy, dividing the subjects into categories. In fact, that is unwholesome idleness. After eating, there is nothing to do, so we say things that fascinate others. Salvation, so where do people come from? Look where the chicken came from? Did the chicken come first or did the egg come first? If there are no chickens, how can there be eggs? And if there are no eggs, there can be no chickens! That's the story of a chicken not following its natural logic. As for humans, did men come first or did women come first? Just as men come first, men come from the mother's womb. If women come first, then there must be a man to get pregnant. Because time has passed for so long, we humans have forgotten what this was like, and no one learns anymore.

All things are fundamentally due to the Buddha Nature, from 'with' it turns into 'without', from nothingness it turns into 'with', born and born suddenly, infinitely transformed; So the more they transform, the more they grow, just like the insects growing in rice, becoming more and more numerous. 'Heaven is One so it is clear.

The land is One so it is peaceful.

This zero is like a circle, neither big nor small, no inside, no outside, no before or after; neither falling in nor falling out. However, all item numbers do not break away from this zero.

People who practice practice return from number one to number zero. At number zero, they can have boundless and boundless effects. Although it is said that ' is the best in all things, ', but when we reach this zero, the number one is no longer there. That is:

If you want to get to zero, you must first unify your mind, don't give rise to false thoughts, only if your mind and body can be single, then there will be inspiration. That's why we often hear: 'That's what it's like to touch the road and communicate with others.' is like that.

After a while, you must practice sitting in a half-lotus position. If your legs no longer hurt like before, you must practice sitting cross-legged. People who cultivate the Way, have enough food and warm clothes, and have enough work to do, should meditate, which is called wandering around the human world. When participating in the first conversation, you need to slowly sharpen it with the utmost care and diligence, focusing on your own nature and working hard. That's why it's called Tham Ngo. However, I want to use the method of making poison work alone. Use one delusion to conquer all other delusions. Use one thought to eliminate all other false thoughts.

Just now I talked about zero, this zero is the path to become Buddha.

Today I tell you this not as a small cause, but as revealing the plan of heaven, revealing the secret of heaven and earth. Talk about the origin of the Buddhas. noi_dung:
Story of Venerable Master Hsuan Hua

The Venerable, dharma name An Tu, pseudonym Do Luan, is the ninth Patriarch of the Quy Nguong Zen lineage, obtained the Dharma from the Great Venerable Hu Van. In addition to the Dharma name Hsuan Hua, he also took the title "Monk in the Tomb" (Monk in the Grave). The Venerable Master's hometown was in Songcheng district, Kietlin province, Manchuria. He was born on March 16, Mau Ngo year (1918), at the end of the Qing Dynasty. His family's name is Bach, his father's name is Phu Hai, his mother's name is Ho. His mother spent her entire life reciting Buddha's name. When she was pregnant, she often prayed to the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas, so on the night before the birth, she dreamed of Amitabha Buddha emitting great light, and immediately gave birth to Him.

From childhood, he followed his mother to practice vegetarianism and recite Buddha's name. At the age of 11, because he saw the great matter of birth and death, human life was too fleeting, he made the great determination to become a monk. When he was ten years old, he bowed to Venerable Thuong Tri as his teacher. At the age of nineteen, his mother passed away, so he went to Tam Duyen Pagoda to ask the Venerable Thuong Tri to become a monk. Then he put on his robe and set up a tent next to his mother's grave to show filial piety. During that time, he bowed to the Avatamsaka Sutra, performed penance, practiced meditation, practiced meditation, and strictly practiced the practice of eating one meal a day. When he mastered his practice, he moved countless villagers around to worship and respect him. His pure practice with sincere devotion also touched the Buddhas, Bodhisattvas, and Dharma Protector Long Thien, causing countless unimaginable miracles to happen. Because those strange stories circulated everywhere, he was called "the strange monk."

In 1946, he came to attend the ceremony of Venerable Hu Van, a monk whom he greatly admired as the North Star of Buddhism. Old Venerable Hu Van knew that he was a dragon statue in the Dharma gate, so he immediately transmitted the Dharma vein, making him the heir, the ninth generation Patriarch of the Quy Ngoc lineage. Counting from the First Patriarch Maha Kasyapa, he is the forty-sixth descendant.

In 1948, he said goodbye to the Venerable Venerable Hu Van and set out to Hong Kong to propagate the Dharma, with the intention of promoting all five sects: Zen, Doctrine, Tantra, Vinaya, and Pure Land to eliminate sectarianism and division. During this time, he restored many ancient pagodas, printed sutras, created Buddha statues, built An Lac Vien Pagoda, Buddhist Lecture Hall, and Tu Hung Pagoda. At the same time, he also preached sutras and sermons, making Buddhism popular in Hong Kong.

By 1959, he observed that Western Buddhism had matured and could spread the true principles of Dharma everywhere, so he asked his disciples to establish at the United States the "Central American Buddhist Association" (which later became the Dharma Realm Buddhist Association). In 1962, responding to the requests of followers in America, he came to America alone and built the Dharma site "Buddhist Lecture Hall" at Cuu Kim Son.

In 1968, he opened a summer course to teach practice and study the Shurangama Sutra. Dozens of students from the University of Washington in Seattle came down to participate and learn about Buddhism. At the end of the course, five Americans begged him to become a monk, marking the opening of the American Buddhist Sangha. From then on, more and more Americans became monks with him, bringing an extremely profound influence on the propagation of Buddhism in the West, as well as on the translation of the scriptures.

Every time he preached the sutras and dharma, he preached deeply but was very easy to understand. Over the past few decades, he has ascended to the throne to preach more than ten thousand times. Hundreds of sutras preached by him have been translated into English; It can be said that he is the one who has translated the most scriptures into English.

In 1973, he founded the International Sutra Translation Institute with the intention of translating "The Tripitaka" into many different languages, allowing Buddha-Dharma to spread everywhere.

In 1974, he founded the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas and established the Dharma Realm University and the State Training Sangha to train talented people in Dharma with international qualifications and standards. He also founded Duc Luong Primary School and Virtue Cultivation High School, with the policy of using education to save and change people's minds. In the following years, he successively established Kim Son Pagoda, Kim Luan Pagoda, Kim Phong Pagoda, Golden Buddha Pagoda, Hoa Nghiem Pagoda, Dharma Realm Pagoda, Amitabha Pagoda, Long Beach Pagoda, Dharma Realm Holy City, Dharma Realm Religious Research Institute, Kim Thanh Pagoda and many other Bodhimandas. He sacrificed himself, tirelessly working hard, setting an example, teaching and preaching the Dharma with the purpose of setting an example to train future generations. He consecrated the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas to be "The Place of Refuge for Buddhists Worldwide." Ordained the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas very seriously, following the six Principles that he practiced from the time he became a monk, which are: no fighting, no greed, no seeking, no self-interest, no selfishness, no lies. Due to his practice and virtue, the City of Ten Thousand Buddhas has become an important Bodhimanda of American Buddhism.

His direction or motto is in the following poem:

Even though it's cold, there's no fate.

Even if you starve to death, don't beg.

Despite being poor, there is no need for help.

Depending on external conditions, but not changing one's will.

Not changing direction, but still depending on external conditions.

So we can maintain the three great Principles:

Derive yourself for Buddhist cause,

Saving people is your duty,

Edit your work Increase.

Whenever you encounter something, understand it.

Understand a principle and practice it.

So we can inherit the Patriarch's bloodline.

Venerable Master Hsuan Hua's meditation and profound wisdom truly opened the path to enlightenment for Sentient Beings of the end of the dharma. The Venerable Master's life has touched and praised us; For example, in the dark night, we encounter the light of Prajna, or in a dark place, we can smell the scent of Buddha's Dharma, or in the dirty mud, a pure lotus blossoms. We have just learned that the realm of a great practitioner is inconceivable.
